title: QueryProvider swallows failed owner-token bootstrap — app renders permanently unauthenticated
description: frontend/src/app/providers/QueryProvider.tsx:29-34: if bootstrapOwnerToken() rejects (backend down/restarting), the catch only console.errors and still calls setReady(true). The app then runs with token=null for the WHOLE session: every write 401s, and because a 401 body is not a SystemMessageList, apiFetch (frontend/src/data/_client/api.ts:34) synthesizes an INTERNAL_ERROR message with no exceptionTraceId, so the user only sees the generic 'Mentés sikertelen — próbáld újra' toast with no trace id and no hint that they are unauthenticated. Only a full reload recovers. Surfaced right after the mezo-rcsy purge (backend was scaled to 0 during it). Fix direction: retry the bootstrap (backoff) and/or surface an explicit 'nincs kapcsolat / jelentkezz be újra' state instead of rendering an unauthenticated app; consider re-bootstrapping on the first 401 from a write.

title: Advisor false pozitívok kiszűrése — TurnVerdictCheck unmarkedClaim pontossága
description:
CÉL: megállapítani, a companion advisor retry-jai közül melyik volt jogos és melyik false pozitív, és a prompt/kontextus melyik hiánya okozza őket.

KIINDULÁS (mezo-prb9 designja közben gyűjtve, élő llm_log_history, 2026-08-02..08-23):
17 streamelt kör / 6 violation-ös verdict / 4 retry (~24%). Mind a 6 violation unmarkedClaim volt (egynél redundantQuestion is).

KÉT GYANÚS FALSE-POZITÍV OSZTÁLY a 6 indoklásból:

(1) A BÍRÓ NEM LÁTJA A TOOL-KIMENETET. A TurnVerdictCheck javadocja ezt v1 korlátként rögzíti ('Tool results are not captured in v1'), és a bíró a 2026-08-23 08:43-as körben szó szerint ki is mondja: '...sem az eszközhívásból (mivel annak kimenete nincs megadva)...'. Vagyis MINDEN tool-ból származó konkrét szám (pl. a 85,536 kg kezdősúly) strukturálisan gyanús a bírónak, akkor is, ha tökéletesen megalapozott. Ez nem hangolási kérdés, hanem hiányzó bemenet.

(2) ÉRTÉKELÉST TÉNYÁLLÍTÁSNAK MINŐSÍT. A 2026-08-18 09:35 és a 2026-08-23 08:43 körben a bíró azért bukatta a választ, mert az a heti 0,347 / 0,366 kg ütemet 'pont a tervezett ütem' / 'megfelelő' minősítéssel illette a 0,8 kg/hét célhoz képest. Ez kvalitatív értékelés, nem kitalált szám — a promptban lévő 'A kontextusban szereplő adatokból számolt/becsült érték alátámasztottnak számít' kitétel elvileg fedné, a gyakorlatban nem fedi.

MÓDSZER: az llm_log_history minden szükséges nyersanyagot tárol — a stream response_text-je az attempt-1, a verdict_check response_text-je a JSON ítélet, a retry response_text-je az attempt-2. Végig kell nézni mind a 6 esetet (és a további gyűlőket) attempt-1/ítélet/attempt-2 hármasával, jogos/false pozitív címkével, és eldönteni, hogy a javítás rontott vagy javított-e a válaszon.

VÁRHATÓ KIMENET: vagy a tool-kimenetek bevezetése a bíró payloadjába (az (1)-re), vagy promptélesítés az értékelés/tényállítás határra (a (2)-re), vagy mindkettő — külön issue-kban. Ez az issue az AUDIT, nem a fix.

Kapcsolódó: mezo-prb9 (UI oldal), ADR 0028 (jelölt spekuláció szemantikája).

title: Companion: üres LLM-válasz megkeményítés + napi súly tool (get_weight_log)
description:
A 2026-08-23 10:43-as élő beszélgetés vizsgálatából (lásd a session diagnózist):

TÜNET 1 — üres asszisztens-buborék. A streamelt kör 0 szöveg-chunkot adott vissza (nincs tool-hívás, nincs hiba), az advisor a ''-t elfogadta (retries=0, degraded=false, 6316 ms), a completeTurn pedig szó nélkül elmentette. A FE üres kártyát renderelt, csak a HIVATKOZOTT/EMLÉKEK sávval (azok az LLM-kör UTÁN kerülnek az auditra).
Backend log bizonyíték: 2026-08-23T10:43:50.384 'Advisor chain took 6316 ms (retries=0, degraded=false)'.

TÜNET 2 — továbbgyűrűzés: az üres asszisztens-sor bekerül a következő kör history-jába (ChatService.toTurns nem szűr) üres AssistantMessage-ként; a Gemini az üres part-ot elutasíthatja, ami a teljes szálat megmérgezi.

TÜNET 3 — nincs finishReason az llm_log_history-ban, ezért nem eldönthető, hogy MAX_TOKENS-in-thinking volt-e az üres candidate oka.

TÜNET 4 — a súlyra csak get_weight_trend létezik (aggregált EWMA); napi mérési pontokat nem lehet lekérni, ezért a 'nézd meg a heti ingadozást' kérdésre a modell nem tudott válaszolni.

SCOPE:
1. blank-guard: üres/whitespace végső válasz ne perzisztálódjon, hanem kezelt SSE error legyen (a sync path is)
2. ChatService.toTurns szűrje ki az üres tartalmú sorokat (védelem a MÁR bent lévő sorra is)
3. finish_reason oszlop az llm_log_history-ba + extractor + DTO + /me AI-napló detail
4. új get_weight_log tool: napi nyers mérések ablakban + routing hint a SYSTEM_PROMPT [Eszköz-útmutató] blokkjában

title: Fuel push bodies poisoned with '(törölt Kamra-item)' — snapshot writer races pantry query
description: The 'Stack · reggeli slot' (and every fuel_slot) push shows '(törölt Kamra-item)' for every item. Root cause: useScheduleSnapshotWriter (notificationScheduleWriter.ts) gates only on useSleepGoal().isPending; usePantry returns stash: [] while unresolved, so when the sleep-goal + protocol queries resolve before the (heaviest) pantry query, projectStackDay falls back to '(törölt Kamra-item)' for every occurrence and the poisoned bodies are PUT to /api/notification/schedule, which AnchorResolver pushes verbatim. Once poisoned it persists: opens where protocol is also unresolved only replace the checkin category. Fix: gate the snapshot on the pantry AND protocol queries having resolved too.
close_reason: Gate added: useScheduleSnapshotWriter now waits for useStack/useProtocol to settle successfully (pending/error flags) before snapshotting; poisoned rows self-heal on next app open after deploy.

title: LLM audit log retention/pruning — a tábla korlátlanul nő, teljes prompt/válasz szöveggel
description: WHY: az ADR 0014 (mezo-2zyu) 'Consequences' szakasza ezt nevezi meg az ELSŐ follow-upként: 'The table only grows. Nothing prunes it yet, and prompts/responses are stored.' A mezo-uakh óta böngészhető felület is van rá (/me/ai-usage), ami növeli a tétet: a sorok most már nem csak nőnek, hanem meg is nyithatók. Egy sor max 3x64000 karakternyi payloadot tárolhat (mezo.llm-log.max-payload-chars), és a prod kulcson ~100 hivas/nap ment. WHAT: retention-politika + pruning. Nyitott döntések, amiket a specnek el kell dontenie: (1) megtartási ablak — fix napszam vagy soronkent eltero (pl. a payload elobb tunik el, mint a koltseg-metaadat)? (2) a payload-oszlopok NULL-ozasa vs. a teljes sor DELETE-je — az elobbi megtartja a koltseg-tortenetet orokre, ami a feature eredeti celja volt (cost attribution), az utobbi egyszerubb; (3) hol fut — @Scheduled cron a techcore.cron mintajara (kapcsolo: mezo.techcore.cron.*), vagy DB-oldali job; (4) a tabla INSERT-only es SZANDEKOSAN nincs rajta is_deleted (az ADR 0014 allo kivetele a soft-delete hazszabaly alol), tehat a pruning HARD DELETE — ezt a dontest a specnek ujra ki kell mondania. FIGYELEM: a created_by nullable ON DELETE SET NULL, tehat a felhasznalo torlese nem viszi el a koltseg-tortenetet; a pruning ne rontsa el ezt a tulajdonsagot. Kapcsolodo: ADR 0014 docs/decisions/0014-llm-call-audit-log.md, tabla docs/features/companion.md '#Backend tables (LLM audit log)'.

design: Extract DERIVED_HEADLINE_TYPES = ['E1RM','SESSION_VOLUME'] — the two types whose headline lives in  rather than in the set — and gate the set-shaped branch on it. WEIGHT/REPS_AT_WEIGHT/TARGET_HIT keep the set form because their headline IS the set. Removed E1RM from the test that encoded the bug and pinned the correct behavior plus a counter-arm for the three set-shaped types.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #111 (merge 2c3888bc). DERIVED_HEADLINE_TYPES gates the set-shaped branch; the test that asserted the defect was corrected.

title: Medal collection: live per-set PR + progression-target medals (derived) + Train medal cabinet
description: Today nothing compares a logged set against either the progression target or the user's records. The mid-workout PR toast is a hardcoded demo (ActiveWorkoutPage.tsx:405 - >=105kg on exercise 0, set 3) and the summary 'PR' suffix derives from a max_strength skill level-up, not a real record. Hitting the Progression-recommended set/rep yields no feedback at all - the driving user complaint. Build a Hevy-style medal system: 4 record types (weight, reps-at-weight, e1RM, session volume) + a mezo-specific TARGET_HIT medal per working set that meets the prescribed weight AND reps. Medals are DERIVED from exercise_set by chronological replay (no materialized table), which requires persisting the prescribed target on the set row. A Train-side medal cabinet surfaces the full dated history; record medals celebrate with a toast, the frequent target medals stay quiet.
design: Derived-replay over a materialized set_medal table (reverses the YAGNI call in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-exercise-records-design.md:123): no drift, free backfill, consistent with ExerciseRecordService. Requires exercise_set.target_weight_kg + target_reps (nullable) so TARGET_HIT is derivable; old rows have null targets so TARGET_HIT accrues only going forward while the 4 record types backfill for free. XP folds into the EXISTING GYM award via GymSignal (revives the dead prBonusXp, which today only fires on the first-ever weighted session) - no new progression source type, no DB CHECK change, no coins.
acceptance_criteria: Logging a set that meets the progression target shows a medal; breaking a record fires a celebration toast naming the previous value and its date; the workout summary lists the session medals; a Train medal cabinet shows the full dated history backfilled from existing set data; both FE modes green (mock needs a seeded record baseline + local evaluator); docs/features/train.md no longer lists PR detection as a scripted demo.

title: Chat answers before tool results are visible: no live tool SSE events + pre-tool narration
description:
The streamed turn makes the companion look like it answers before its tools run.

Three contributing causes:
1. The model narrates BEFORE calling a tool ('Nezzuk meg...', 'Most megprobalom megnezni...'). That preamble streams first and is persisted as part of the answer. ChatService.SYSTEM_PROMPT (service/ChatService.java:46-69) has no rule against pre-tool narration.
2. Tool chips and refs are back-filled at the very end. The wire carries exactly three events - delta/done/error (service/ChatStreamService.java:42-44) - and the FE's streaming bubble passes only {role, ts, text} (frontend ChatPage.tsx:73), so chips (ChatMessage.tsx:47) can only come from the terminal done payload. The whole tool phase renders as undifferentiated ThinkingDots.
3. At done the FE discards the streamed draft and renders the authoritative row (chatHooks.ts:97,102-104), which CompanionAdvisorChain.review (advisor/CompanionAdvisorChain.java:48-71) may have entirely rewritten in a non-streamed corrective round - so the text visibly swaps.

Verified NOT the cause: Spring AI's streaming tool loop is correct - GoogleGenAiChatModel.internalStream recurses with the tool result and streams the continuation.
acceptance_criteria: New 'tool' SSE event on the companion stream contract (api/feature/companion), emitted from the RecordingToolCallback choke point as each tool actually executes, with the same pre-baked 'name(args)' label as CompanionMapper; FE renders live tool chips during the stream; SYSTEM_PROMPT forbids pre-tool narration (call the tool first, answer from the result); backend + FE tests in both modes; docs/features/companion.md streaming section updated
close_reason: live 'tool' SSE event from the RecordingToolCallback/ToolCallAudit choke point + anti-preamble system prompt rule + FE live chips on the in-flight draft bubble; 5 tasks, all reviewed, whole-branch review clean

title: get_recipes cannot find a recipe by its name or ingredients
description:
FuelTools.matchesRecipeFilter (tools/FuelTools.java:372-386) matches only slot/category/tag/starred/fitsFor and deliberately NOT the recipe name. The comment cites 'spec R1', but that section does not exist anywhere in docs/ (nor in git history) - the real 'Recipe R1' in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-companion-tool-context-expansion.md:50 is the generic hub-tool boilerplate pattern, unrelated to filtering. So the exclusion is undocumented and unjustified.

Consequences:
- 'a smoothie collagen a receptek kozul' -> 'Receptek - "smoothie collagen": nincs adat' even when that recipe exists (real chat, 2026-07-29).
- ingredients[].name is in the same RecipeResponse the tool already holds, so 'mit fozzek csirkevel' / 'van valami turos' can never match either. role is unused too.
- Even a correct literal name cannot work reliably: a two-word needle is matched as ONE substring, so 'smoothie collagen' misses a recipe named 'Collagen Smoothie'.

Incidental defect in the same method: the starred branch (:380-382) matches bidirectionally (k.contains(needle) || needle.contains(k)), so any short needle that is a substring of 'csillagos'/'kedvenc'/'starred' (e.g. 'a', 'cs', 'red') matches EVERY starred recipe.

The filter-miss branch (:320) has zero test coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Token-based, accent-folded (NFD) scored matching over name + ingredient names + tags + category + slot + role + fitsFor; multi-word needles match in any order; best match wins the detail render; starred keyword match is exact-token (no bidirectional substring); @Tool/@ToolParam descriptions state what is actually matched (companion_tool_conventions.md); ITs cover name match, ingredient match, multi-word any-order match, the starred regression and the miss branch; docs/features/companion.md tool catalog updated
close_reason: scored accent-folded token match over name/ingredients/tags/category/slot/role/fitsFor; all-token hits win; best scorer renders detail; starred whole-token only; 5 ITs, 4 verified red-then-green

title: Companion is blind to scheduled sport on a given date
description:
get_training_plan renders only gym + running for today/tomorrow/week/date: TrainTools.dayContentLine (tools/TrainTools.java:276-295) never consults sport_schedule_slot, and SportService is not even injected (TrainTools.java:54-69). A volleyball evening renders 'gym: pihenonap', and the NO_DATA guard (:250, :263) can claim 'nincs adat' for a day that has a scheduled sport slot.

ContextSnapshotAssembler is asymmetric for the same reason: tomorrowLine (:283-311) adds sport + run, todayLine (:259-274) is gym-only. So 'Ma' under-reports and the model has to derive today's sport from the trailing raw weekly 'sport-rend' pattern (:230-234) - exactly the hallucination path the dated resolution was meant to remove.

Repro (real chat, 2026-07-29): 'mai napomrol mit latsz?' listed only the Full Body gym day; only when pushed with 'sport?' did the model derive '18:00, 120 perc' from the weekly pattern.
acceptance_criteria: get_training_plan scope=today|tomorrow|week|date renders the date's sport schedule slots (sport, time, kind, duration); a sport-only day is never 'nincs adat' and never bare 'pihenonap'; ContextSnapshotAssembler.todayLine renders sport + run symmetrically with tomorrowLine; focused ITs cover a sport-only day and a gym+sport day; docs/features/companion.md updated
close_reason: get_training_plan renders the date's sport slots; todayLine/tomorrowLine unified into one dayLine; shared ToolText.sportLine; 5 ITs verified red-then-green

title: LLM call audit log (llm_log_history) — decorator-captured, per-call token/cost/entity trail
description: WHY: The Google AI Studio spend dashboard surfaced ~100 Gemini calls/day with zero server-side visibility into which feature/model/entity drove them (the cost scare that triggered this). We have NO central record of what we actually send/receive — debugging a bad LLM turn, attributing cost, or auditing calls all require reconstructing from logs we don't keep. WHAT: An append-only llm_log_history table capturing EVERY LLM call (chat/vision/tool/smart via CompanionLlm + embeddings via EmbeddingPort + proactive crons) in one table with a call_kind discriminator. Captured via two @Primary decorator adapters (LoggingCompanionLlm, LoggingEmbeddingPort) wrapping the real Gemini adapters — reading the REAL served modelVersion + usageMetadata token breakdown from ChatResponse (which .call().content() currently discards). Async non-blocking write (ApplicationEvent -> @Async @EventListener, own REQUIRES_NEW tx, success AND error), stream-end capture for SSE. Cost stored honestly: full token breakdown + a frozen price-snapshot (jsonb) from a mezo.llm-log.pricing config table, cost_usd computed from the snapshot so it never drifts. Entity-level attribution: user+call_kind automatic (principal + port method), feature/operation a small caller tag, entity_kind/entity_id optional. Feature switch mezo.feature.llm-log.enabled (off -> no decorator, zero overhead). INSERT-only (deliberate deviation from the is_deleted house default — audit rows are never mutated). v1 = DB table only (psql/SQL); read-API/UI + retention pruning are later/separate. Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-llm-call-audit-log-design.md

title: Fuel/Profil NaN: deployed backend version-skew (régi kód szolgálja ki az új FE-t)
description:
A deployed PWA-n a Profil oldal Alaphő·NEAT és Betábl. mozgás mezői NaN-t mutatnak, a Fuel 'Mai cél' kártyáról eltűnt az Alaphő/Mozgás/Deficit bontás.

Gyökérok (kód-szinten cáfolhatatlan): a deployed FRONTEND az új mezo-eujg build (az Alap-TDEE split kártyát rendereli: Alaphő·NEAT / Betábl. mozgás / Fenntartó·Katch), de a deployed BACKEND még RÉGI, mezo-eujg (dc040749) ELŐTTI kódot futtat. A régi TdeeBootstrap DTO alakja {bmr, tdee, pal, formula, computedAt}; az új {bmr, neat, neatBaselineKcal, weeklyEatKcalPerDay, tdee, formula, computedAt}.

Bizonyíték: nincs sem @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) a generált DTO-n, sem globális default-property-inclusion=non_null → új kód a null mezőt is kiírná ("neatBaselineKcal": null → FE Math.round(null)=0). A képen NaN (=undefined=hiányzó kulcs) → a backend válaszban NINCS is neatBaselineKcal → régi backend-kód. tdee=2935 (régi mező) még jön. Fuel: neat=undefined → deriveDailyBudget statikus ágra esik → activity=0,balance=0 → staticEnergy=true → a chipek elrejtve.

A jelenlegi kód (main/0.132.0) HELYES; a k8s manifest mezo-backend:0.132.0-ra mutat (új kód), de a FUTÓ backend pod nyilván nem az → ArgoCD sync / rollout akadt el (valószínűleg új pod nem Ready: OOM 1Gi limit / Liquibase migráció / ImagePull). A GoalReevaluateRunner (@Profile demodata) induláskor újraértékeli az owner-goalt és friss tdeeBootstrap-ot ír — tehát ha az új backend pod elindul, magától reconcile-ódik, kézi evaluate nélkül.

Fix: a mezo namespace-ben ki kell deríteni, miért nem fut a backend:0.132.0 pod, és el kell indítani. Nincs kubectl kontextus a fejlesztői session-ben — a diagnózis a user gépén futó kubectl-t igényel.
notes:
CONFIRMED root cause (via kubectl over Tailscale): NOT ops-only — a real release bug.

Live cluster state: backend Deployment desired image 0.132.0, but the RUNNING/Ready pod was the OLD 0.130.0 RS; the 0.132.0 pod was CrashLoopBackOff (162 restarts / 13h). ArgoCD app = Synced/Degraded.

Crash cause (0.132.0 boot log): com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.UnrecognizedPropertyException: Unrecognized field 'pal' (class TdeeBootstrapJson) ... FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES. The live goal.tdee_bootstrap jsonb still held the OLD shape {bmr,pal,tdee,formula,computedAt}. dc040749 (mezo-eujg) renamed pal->neat + added neatBaselineKcal/weeklyEatKcalPerDay on the record but (a) did NOT add @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) and (b) shipped no data migration. GoalReevaluateRunner (the intended self-heal) can't run because reading the stale goal to re-evaluate it IS the crash. Catch-22. Local didn't crash because its tdee_bootstrap was NULL.

RESOLUTION (Part A, prod unblocked + VERIFIED): pg_dump backup of goal table taken (scratchpad goal-table-backup-20260727-live.sql + restore-tdee snippet). Then: UPDATE goal SET tdee_bootstrap=NULL WHERE tdee_bootstrap ? 'pal'  (hit 2 rows: active + 1 soft-deleted). Deleted the crashlooping pod -> 0.132.0 booted in 22s, rolled out successfully, old 0.130.0 gone. Log: 'Re-evaluated 1 non-archived owner goal(s)'. DB + GET /api/goals now return fresh {bmr,neat,neatBaselineKcal,weeklyEatKcalPerDay,tdee,formula}. NaN gone; Fuel dynamic breakdown restored. TDEE 2935->3763 (expected: new model adds weeklyEat explicitly).

title: Macro dim: forgive protein overshoot (fitness-app policy)
description: The Kcal & makró dimension scores with symmetric total-variation deviation: protein ABOVE the target share is penalized exactly like a deficit (e.g. the lecsó recipe: P 43% vs 27% target -> 68). For a fitness app, energy shifted INTO protein should not be punished. Add a configurable protein-surplus penalty factor (mezo.meal.scoring.macro-protein-surplus-penalty, default 0.0 = forgiven; 1.0 = old symmetric behavior): deviation = (surplusP*k + deficitP + |dC| + |dF|)/2. Carb/fat deficits still count (a pure-protein meal is still not a balanced meal). Update the LLM prompt's macro-dimension description so prose does not scold protein. Cached recipe envelopes will regenerate once (numeric mismatch) - expected.

title: FE error triad: ErrorBoundary + Toast system + standard mutation onError
description: The biggest user-facing gap, all verified. State: NO ErrorBoundary anywhere in src/ and react-error-boundary is not a dependency - a render-time exception blanks the whole PWA. Query errors do NOT blank (throwOnError defaults false) but are fully silent: features/ has ZERO isError reads, no .catch around mutateAsync (.then(close) pattern at EditGoalSheet.tsx:68,88, AttachPlanSheet.tsx:139, BiometricSheet.tsx:41), and data/ has exactly one onError (checkinHooks.ts:14 - console.error only). Failed writes (meal log, workout save, goal upsert) give the user zero feedback in real mode. Additionally ~7 files hand-roll setTimeout auto-hide toasts: ActiveWorkoutPage, MesocyclePlannerPage, RunningBlockBuilderPage, CheckInSheet, ImportItemSheet, QuickInputSheet, ChatPage + FuelStackPage.tsx:61-68 (note: PRToast.tsx itself is purely presentational - show/dismiss lives in LevelUpProvider, manual-dismiss; earlier audit miscited it). Build: (a) app-level ErrorBoundary + per-tab boundary under the Outlet with a fallback matching the existing GhostState/ScreenSkeleton vocabulary (the error leg of the loading/empty/error triad is simply missing), (b) ToastProvider + useToast (app/ or shared/), (c) standard mutation onError -> toast wired at the data layer, (d) replace the hand-rolled toasts. Update docs/features/_platform docs + frontend_conventions.md in the same change.
notes: Done, merged 45dce1b. Delivered: shared/lib/toastBus (React-free pub/sub) + shared/ui/ToastProvider+useToast (single host in AppLayout, .toast CSS reuse, kind-tinted, role=status, 3.2s auto-hide) + shared/ui/ErrorBoundary (app-level in main.tsx with reload fallback + tab-level in AppLayout with resetKey=pathname) + QueryProvider MutationCache.onError -> HU error toast with exceptionTraceId (every failed write surfaces; per-mutation handlers compose). SCOPE CALL: FuelStackPage protocol card + PRToast stay feature-local — they are purpose-built rich confirmations, not toast duplicates (generic replacement would lose information); the ~7 other setTimeout sites are inline flashes, not floating toasts — noted for .11 as optional case-by-case migration. Docs: _platform-design-system 2.7 + frontend_conventions 7a + _platform-data-layer provider note. Gate: build + 842/842 both modes (7 new tests).

title: CI test job: both FE modes + backend ITs (Testcontainers) as blocking gate
description: Verified: .github/workflows/ contains only deploy.yml which builds (pnpm build; mvn clean package -DskipTests) and intentionally runs ZERO tests (header comment cites mezo-oa3, tests are a local pre-push gate). Consequence: the dualMode.guard.test.ts machine guard, the both-test-modes gate, and all 71 backend ITs never run automatically - nothing blocks a violating merge to main. Add .github/workflows/ci.yml on push/PR: (a) pnpm test AND VITE_USE_MOCK=true pnpm test (both modes must be green per CLAUDE.md), (b) backend ./mvnw clean test -Dmezo.test.use-testcontainers=true (throwaway Postgres, works on ubuntu-latest), (c) order cheap static checks (lint job from the quick-wins issue) before the expensive test job. Decide the deploy relation: keep deploy.yml fast but gate it on ci success (workflow_run or shared workflow) vs keep fully independent. This single change converts every existing manual gate into a blocking one - the biggest enforcement lever found by the audit. Document in docs/infrastructure/ + the enforcement ADR.
notes: Done: ci.yml gained test-frontend (both vitest modes) + test-backend (Testcontainers ITs). First full run green end-to-end (run 28591255796: all 4 jobs success). Deploy-gating decision recorded in ADR 0007: deploys stay independent (fix-forward beats delaying releases). Bonus: the gate immediately caught the 3 raw @SpringBootTest classes failing under Testcontainers — fixed forward under mezo-ah18.14(a).

title: CI quick wins: contract-drift check + Liquibase lint + lint-docs (advisory)
description: Three cheap machine gates, <1h total, in a new lightweight lint/ci job (SEPARATE from deploy.yml so deploy stays fast per mezo-oa3). (a) Contract drift: regenerate (cd api/generate && npm run generate:api; cd frontend && pnpm generate:api) then git diff --exit-code api/openapi.yml frontend/src/data/_client/api.gen.ts. Verified: backend cannot drift (openapi-generator-maven-plugin regenerates api.dto/api.controller from ../api/openapi.yml every build) but the FE api.gen.ts is manual-only, and a stale fragments->openapi.yml merge silently feeds BOTH sides the same stale contract. (b) scripts/lint-liquibase.mjs (mirror lint-docs.mjs style): enforce filename regex ^\d{12}_mezo-[a-z0-9]+_.+\.sql$, constraint-name prefixes pk_/fk_/uq_/ck_/idx_, and FAIL on INSERT INTO (seed data must be Java @Profile("demodata"), never SQL). (c) Run node scripts/lint-docs.mjs in CI - block on ERROR, advisory on STALE initially (git-drift staleness has false positives), tighten later. Include an ADR in docs/decisions/ for the enforcement direction (covers this + the CI test job + ESLint + ArchUnit issues) and update docs/infrastructure/.
notes: Done, merged to main (328aad8), first live ci run green (run 28589395977). ci.yml: lint job (lint-docs --errors-only + new lint-liquibase.mjs) + contract-drift job (fragment merge + FE api.gen.ts regen, git diff gate — verified zero drift locally AND in CI). lint-liquibase negative-tested against 10 violation types. title: Supplement w/o dose blocks pantry edit (400) + recipe ingredient amount not typeable
description:
Two fixes surfaced by supplements-as-recipe-ingredients (mezo-3vu4):
1) BACKEND BUG: PantryService.validatePerKind hard-requires 'dose' for all non-food kinds. A gram-based supplement (protein powder: per/unit, no dose, per mezo-1za9) then fails PUT/POST with 400, so editing its ADAG (per) silently reverts. Fix: non-food requires dose OR per.
2) FE: recipe editor per-ingredient amount is +/- only; make it a typeable numeric input (decimals) keeping the +/- steppers, so exact grams can be entered (also resolves the '/adag vs /100g' confusion for supplements).
notes: Root cause (backend): PantryService.validatePerKind hard-required 'dose' for non-food → a gram-based supplement (per/unit, no dose) 400'd on PUT, so ADAG edits reverted. Fix: non-food requires dose OR per. FE: recipe ingredient amount now a typeable AmountField (decimals, keeps ±10 steppers). TDD: PantryServiceIT +2 (create/update gram supplement) + AddPantryItemSheet per round-trip + 2 RecipeEditor amount tests. Backend 412/412, FE 741/741 both modes + build green. Visually verified. Note: the '25→100 reverts' only fully clears on the deployed backend after a redeploy.

title: [bug] Recipe editor resolves ingredient name+macros from static mock seed → UUID + 0 macros in real mode
description: RecipeEditorView resolves each draft line's display name + live macro contribution via useRecipes().ingredients, which is the STATIC mock-seed import (recipeHooks.ts:27) even in real mode. close_reason: Fixed: RecipeEditorView + RecipeDetailView resolve ingredient name/macros from usePantry() (dual-mode) instead of the static mock-seed useRecipes().ingredients; removed the footgun seed field from useRecipes() entirely. No logged/status link between VolleyballSession (schedule slot) and SportSession (logged record). Log mutation only invalidates ['train','sportSessions'] (trainHooks.ts:323), which the hero doesn't depend on; mock-mode log is a no-op. Fix: derive 'logged today' (match by today's date + sport) and switch hero + weekly row to a done state; make mock log append to the sessions store via setQueryData.

title: Running block currentWeek=0 → 'aktuális hét nincs a tervben' for a plan starting today
description: RunningService.applyUpsert stores the client currentWeek (0 for new blocks) and activateBlock never recomputes it (mesocycle does, via clampWeek). A block created+activated today shows HÉT 0/8 and 'Az aktuális hét (0) nincs a tervben' because weeks are 1-indexed. Fix: derive currentWeek=clampWeek(startDate,weeks) on create/update, heal invalid currentWeek on read so existing 0-blocks self-heal, mirror in mock. weeks 1-indexed; clampWeek already exists in TrainService.

title: Builder shell layout: sticky breadcrumb double-offset (overlaps header) + content bleeds under translucent tab bar
description: Two layout bugs visible on the run builder (and shared by all .sticky-top builders: Running/Meso builder+planner, ActiveWorkout). (1) .sticky-top { top: 54px } stacks on top of .screen-content { padding-top: 54px }, so the breadcrumb pins ~54px BELOW the status bar instead of directly under it (measured: content top 63px, breadcrumb 117px); because it drops out of its flow position the following header (eyebrow+title) overlaps it on scroll -> 'szétcsúszik'. Fix: .sticky-top top 54px->0 (default + the safe-area media query at ~line 329), since the scrollport already starts below the status bar/notch via padding-top. (2) .tab-bar background rgba(10,15,20,0.75) is too translucent, so the teal bottom CTA bleeds through the tab bar while scrolling ('bemegy a menü alá'); padding-bottom:96px DOES stop the content above the bar at the very end (CTA bottom 813 < tab-bar top 853). Fix: raise the tab-bar background opacity so content fades behind it (keep the blur). Verify with Playwright that all 5 sticky-top screens + a normal screen still look right.
close_reason: Fixed in prototype.css: .sticky-top top 54px->0 (default + safe-area media query) removes the double status-bar offset so the breadcrumb pins directly under the status bar and the header no longer overlaps it; .tab-bar background 0.75->0.92 so scrolling content (teal CTA) fades behind the bar instead of bleeding through. Verified with Playwright on the live builder (breadcrumb top 63 = status bar bottom; header below; CTA absorbed by bar). 377 FE tests x2 modes + build green.

title: Fix: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading weeks)' crash creating a new run plan (REAL mode)
description: Creating a new run plan crashes the builder at RunWeekEditor.tsx:30 (structure.weeks.find on undefined). Root cause: createBlock -> saveRunningBlock(null,newDraft) -> runningApi.create; real-mode saveMutation.onSuccess only invalidate() (async refetch, no synchronous cache insert), then navigates to /train/futas/:id immediately; builder mounts on a stale list -> block undefined -> draft {} -> RunWeekEditor renders with structure undefined and throws. Mock mode is immune (upsertMock setQueryData synchronous). Fix: create onSuccess does qc.setQueryData(['running','blocks']) synchronously in real mode too; builder guards missing structure (loading state); RunWeekEditor/RunSessionCard guard structure?.weeks. Add a create->builder IT/regression test. Shipped together with the redesign but is an independent fix.
close_reason: Fixed in Task 5 (91a6e8f5): synchronous setQueryData insert on real-mode create + RunWeekEditor structure guard; regression test runningHooks.test.ts. Spec+quality reviewed.

title: Backend stack: Java/Spring Boot (not Supabase-direct)
description: DECISION (leaning, finalize at Phase 2). Backend = Java/Spring Boot instead of the handoff's Supabase-direct default. Rationale: solo dev is a Spring Boot expert; the domain is heavy (mesocycle volume calc w/ provenance, pattern engine, cross-load, ~69 entities, scheduled jobs) and fits Spring's strengths (JPA/Hibernate, Liquibase, Spring Security JWT, @Scheduled/Quartz, transactions). Phase 2: frontend mock-hooks swap to Spring Boot REST API -> Postgres (same hook interface; frontend unchanged). Phase 3 AI: Spring AI (multi-provider LLM, pgvector vector store, RAG, function calling, chat memory); optional Python sidecar only if multi-agent graph orchestration gets complex. Deploy: Vercel (frontend) + Spring Boot container on Cloud Run (scale-to-zero) + managed Postgres (Neon/Supabase-DB). Trade-off accepted: lose all-serverless-free simplicity; re-derive schema in Liquibase/JPA from 04-data-model + Phase-3 arch doc instead of using handoff Supabase DDL/RLS/Edge blueprints. Does NOT affect Phase 1 (mock). Repo structure (root frontend vs frontend/+backend/ split) to be decided at Phase 2.
close_reason: Finalized in Phase 2 design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-phase2-backend-design.md): Java/Spring Boot 4.x + Maven + Postgres, symmetric monorepo (frontend/ + backend/), single-user thin auth + app-level ownership, TanStack Query swap. Driving epic: mezo-v67.

title: LlmCallListIT midnight flake: period=DAY window vs now-minus-minutes seeding
description: backend/src/test/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/llmlog/controller/LlmCallListIT.java testListCalls_shouldFlagMoreRows_whenWindowSmallerThanThePeriod seeds 12 rows at Instant.now().minus(i, MINUTES) for i=0..11 and then asserts period=DAY returns all 12. period=DAY is bounded at LOCAL (Europe/Budapest) midnight, so any CI run in the first 11 minutes after local midnight drops the rows that fell into the previous day. Observed on PR #253 run 32782119433 at 22:06Z (= 00:06 local): 'Expected size: 12 but was: 7'. Fix: seed at deterministic offsets inside the current local day (e.g. anchor to local midnight + N seconds) instead of now-minus-minutes, or freeze the clock. title: Graph nodes are never retracted: un-confirmed pattern / deleted goal keeps an active node forever
description: W2.2 follow-up (mezo-b3pp.7 final review, Important). Promotion is one-way: (a) confirming a pattern creates a PATTERN node, but re-deciding it as rejected/monitoring fires no event and never archives the node, so the graph keeps asserting something the user explicitly rejected; (b) GoalService.deleteGoal soft-deletes a goal but leaves its GOAL node active (the status path demotes, the delete path does not); (c) a soft-deleted knowledge_fact keeps its PREFERENCE node. GraphPromotionService.reconcile cannot heal any of these — it iterates only confirmed patterns and non-deleted facts/goals, so rows that leave those sets are never revisited. Fix before W2.4 (mezo-b3pp.9) renders nodes into the prompt: archive on retraction (event or reconcile-side sweep over the complement sets). Related: mezo-b3pp.10 (W2.5 maintenance job) is the natural home for the sweep half.

title: Graph promotion ignores knowledge_fact.includeInPrompt — an opted-out fact still becomes a PREFERENCE node
description: W2.2 follow-up (mezo-b3pp.7 final review, Important). GraphPromotionService.promoteFact does not filter on KnowledgeFactEntity.includeInPrompt, the user's explicit 'do not inject this into the prompt' switch (settable via KnowledgeFactService.update). A fact the user excluded still becomes an active PREFERENCE node, and W2.4's [Osszefuggesek] traversal would render it back into the system prompt. Harmless today (nothing renders graph nodes yet) but MUST be settled before W2.4 (mezo-b3pp.9). Options: filter promotion on includeInPrompt and archive the node when it flips false, or make the deliberate decision explicit in the spec + docs/features/companion.md.

title: W1.5 follow-up: activity_note/checkin_note vectors go stale on source edit and orphan on source delete
description:
W1.5 (mezo-b3pp.5) ships activity_note/checkin_note as WRITE-ONCE kinds: the nightly NoteEmbeddingCatchUp is their only writer and it calls MemoryEmbeddingWriter.writeNote -> the insert-only write(...). Two honest gaps documented in docs/features/journal.md 9:
(a) editing an activity_log.text / check_in.note row after it was embedded leaves the ORIGINAL vector standing (the sweep skips rows that already have a vector);
(b) soft-deleting a source row does NOT remove its vector, so deleted content stays recallable in chat — unlike journal_entry, which has deleteJournalEmbedding (IDENT-3 honesty gap; the delete half is the sharper of the two).

Fix shape: in the nightly pass compare the stored memory_embedding.content against the source text and re-embed on drift; reap vectors whose source row is no longer live.

HARD CONSTRAINT for whoever implements this: uq_memory_embedding_kind_ref_id is a PLAIN (non-partial) unique index, so a soft-deleted vector keeps occupying its (kind, ref_id) slot. Any re-write of a note vector MUST go through MemoryEmbeddingWriter.upsert (which reads MemoryEmbeddingRepository.findByKindAndRefIdIncludingDeleted and revives the row), never the insert-only write — otherwise every nightly run re-selects the row, burns an embedding call, hits the constraint, logs a warn, and repeats forever. Same trap W1.2 (mezo-b3pp.2) hit.

title: pnpm test:visual:update silently no-ops under maxDiffPixels; the visual gate misses small discrete changes
description:
Two linked halves of one harness gap, found while shipping mezo-b3pp.2 (the Napzaras went from 5 acts to 6, so the progress-dot row gained a dot).

1) 'pnpm test:visual:update' runs Playwright 1.60's bare --update-snapshots, which defaults to preset 'changed'. That only rewrites a golden when the diff EXCEEDS maxDiffPixels (120, frontend/tests/visual/playwright.config.ts). The 5->6 dot change differs by only 45px (ritual-arrival) / 90px (ritual-harvest) out of 420640, so the update run reported '43 passed' and silently left the STALE goldens in place. It took a hash-diff against git to notice; the honest rebaseline needed --update-snapshots=all.

2) The same threshold means CI's test-visual job would have gone GREEN against the old 5-dot linux baselines. For these screens the gate protects against gross layout breakage but not against a small discrete element changing (one progress dot, a small icon, a short label) -- exactly the class of regression an act insertion is.

Fix candidates: pin the test:visual:update script to --update-snapshots=all; and lower maxDiffPixels (or add per-screen overrides for the progress-dot-bearing shots) so a one-element change actually fails the compare.

title: PatternDetectionServiceIT.testDetect_shouldFreezeUserJudgedRow_whenConfirmed flakes ~50% on linux CI (1us rounding)
description:
PatternEntity.lastDetectedAt defaults to Instant.now() (entity field initializer, PatternEntity.java:128). On linux Instant.now() carries NANOsecond precision; Postgres timestamptz ROUNDS to microseconds, while the test does truncatedTo(ChronoUnit.MICROS), which FLOORS. Whenever the sub-microsecond remainder is >= 500ns the two disagree by exactly 1us and the assertion at PatternDetectionServiceIT.java:269 fails:

  expected: 2026-08-21T19:11:23.185955Z
   but was: 2026-08-21T19:11:23.185956Z

That makes the test roughly a coin flip on ubuntu-latest CI, while it is ~always green on darwin (macOS Instant.now() is already microsecond-resolution, so the truncate is a no-op). Observed failing CI run 32516755749 on feat/evening-reflection while the identical 2096-test suite passed locally on darwin.

Fix options: (a) round instead of truncate in the test, (b) compare with isCloseTo/within(1, MICROS), or (c) better, stop the drift at the source by having the entity default to Instant.now().truncatedTo(ChronoUnit.MICROS) the way RitualService already does for closedAt. Check whether other entities with Instant.now() field initializers share the same latent flake.

Found while shipping mezo-b3pp.2 (W1.2 evening reflection); unrelated to that slice.

description: CI run 32500254612 (branch feat/hermes-skill-fixes, docs-only) failed this single test out of 2070 at line 269 (assertion). Likely timing/ordering flake (frozen row when confirmed). Reproduce with -Dmezo.test.use-testcontainers=true in a loop; fix the race or the assertion.

comments.author: mrkuhne
comments.text:
Root-caused and FIXED (merge 6e509ea4, commit 58f925a7, PR #228). Not a race or an ordering flake: every lastDetectedAt write used a bare Instant.now(). On linux that carries NANOsecond resolution, while timestamptz stores micros and ROUNDS — the test truncates. When the sub-microsecond remainder is >= 500ns the re-read row sits 1us ahead of the persisted one:

  expected: 2026-08-21T19:11:23.185955Z
   but was: 2026-08-21T19:11:23.185956Z

macOS never reproduces it (Instant.now() is already microsecond-resolution there, so the truncate is a no-op) — which is why the same 2096-test suite was green locally and red on CI. Fixed at the source in all three write paths plus the sibling carrying the same latent bug: PatternEntity.lastDetectedAt, PatternDetectionService:139, HypothesisPipelineService:325, PatternEventEntity.occurredAt now truncate to micros (the RitualService.close precedent). PR #228 went green on linux including test-backend.

NOTE: 58f925a7's commit message cites 'mezo-mfmb', which is not a real id — I misread a truncated bd create output. The real ids are this issue and its duplicate mezo-csew. The commit is already on main so the message stands uncorrected.

title: Feedback batch GET at the 200-id cap can exceed Tomcat's default 8 KB header limit
description:
W4.1 (mezo-b3pp.15) ships FEEDBACK_MAX_IDS=200 in frontend/src/data/feedback/feedbackApi.ts, comma-joined into the GET /api/companion/feedback query string. 200 uuids = 7399 chars, so the request line is ~7.45 KB before the Authorization: Bearer <jwt> header and the browser's own headers. Spring Boot's Tomcat default server.max-http-request-header-size is 8 KB and the repo sets no override (grep max-http backend/src/main/resources -> nothing).

CompanionController.listMessages returns the WHOLE conversation with no window, so chat_message is the kind that realistically reaches 200 assistant rows. At that point Tomcat rejects with a bare 400 (no SystemMessageList body), useDualQuery degrades to realEmpty, and every chip on the page silently reads unvoted — then the invalidate after the next vote reverts the chip the user just tapped. IDENT-3-compliant but a silent whole-page loss.

Fix: either set server.max-http-request-header-size: 16KB in application.yml, or lower FEEDBACK_MAX_IDS to ~120. Found by the W4.1 final whole-branch review.

title: Backend CI flake: PatternDetectionServiceIT timestamp rounding by 1 microsecond
description: The full backend CI on run 32254631832 failed only in PatternDetectionServiceIT.testDetect_shouldFreezeUserJudgedRow_whenConfirmed: expected lastDetectedAt ...644685Z but PostgreSQL returned ...644686Z. The test truncates the in-memory Instant to ChronoUnit.MICROS, while PostgreSQL timestamptz rounds fractional microseconds. Make the assertion deterministic by deriving the persisted value (or applying PostgreSQL-equivalent rounding), and add a boundary case with nanos >= 500.

title: MemoryObservatoryService under-reports embedding kinds beyond daily_summary/chat_turn
description: MemoryObservatoryService.overview (backend/src/main/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/companion/service/MemoryObservatoryService.java:131-136) builds MemoryEmbeddingCounts by counting only kind=daily_summary and kind=chat_turn via memoryEmbeddingRepository.countByCreatedByAndKind. The memory_embedding.kind CHECK was widened to ten values in W1.1 (mezo-b3pp.1, migration 202608181610_mezo-b3pp.1_expand_memory_embedding_kinds.sql): chat_turn, daily_summary, weekly_summary, monthly_summary, journal_entry, reflection, gratitude, decision, activity_note, checkin_note. W1.1 already populates journal_entry, and none of its counts surface on the /insights/memoria memory observatory L1 read — the observatory silently under-reports the vector store's real size, and it will get worse as W1.2-W1.5 (reflection/gratitude/decision/activity_note/checkin_note) land their own writers. Widening MemoryEmbeddingCounts (the DTO) is a contract change (api/feature/companion/companion.yml) and therefore out of scope for the W1.1 slice itself -- flagged for its own follow-up rather than folded into mezo-b3pp.1's fix wave. Fix: widen MemoryEmbeddingCounts to carry all ten narrative kinds (or a kind->count map) and update MemoryObservatoryService.overview's l1.embeddings assembly accordingly; update the FE memory observatory consumer + docs/features/companion.md's memory-observatory section together (contract-first per api_contract_conventions.md).

description:
The iOS list-language redesign (mezo-e26w, ADR 0026, 2026-08-11) rewrote nearly all of /today's DOM/CSS (the .segtabs pills -> .td-seg segmented control, the full-bleed briefing band -> MezoChip, every row -> TodayRow/.td-row). The implementation plan's first pass skipped the design spec's goldens step (spec §11); a follow-up task (17) closed the darwin half: `cd frontend && pnpm test:visual:update` regenerated the six today-{reggel,nap,este}-{light,dark}-darwin.png snapshots and each was eyeballed against the new DOM (compact Mezo chip, one boxed section per header, five distinct row icons on the morning routine).

Remaining scope, narrowed to the linux half only: the today-*-linux.png baselines are produced solely by .github/workflows/update-visual-baselines.yml (not locally) and have not been regenerated yet. Trigger that workflow on this branch/PR (gh workflow run update-visual-baselines.yml -r <branch>) and confirm CI's visual step goes green.

title: Unify Today's TodayRow/TodayList list language with shared/ui/ItemRow
description: Today's iOS list language (mezo-e26w, ADR 0026) shipped a new Today-local components/{TodayRow,TodayList,TodayStats}.tsx instead of touching shared/ui/ItemRow, so Today and Fuel's "Mai" window flow (features/fuel/components/WindowIsland.tsx) + the Me routine editor (features/me/pages/RoutineEditorPage.tsx) now speak two different row languages. This is a deliberate, guarded trade (frontend/src/features/today/todayScope.test.ts asserts no Today component imports shared/ui/ItemRow) recorded in ADR 0026 (docs/decisions/0026-today-ios-list-language.md) and the design spec's §7 scope boundary (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-today-ios-redesign-design.md). Follow-up: if the .td-* iOS list idiom (TodayRow's tick/button/chevron/none accessory shapes, the hairline-separated TodayList box) proves out, promote it into shared/ui and migrate Fuel's WindowIsland + the Me routine editor onto it, retiring the older ItemRow card language (or vice versa if ItemRow's shape wins out) -- so the app goes back to ONE row language. Update docs/features/_platform-design-system.md + docs/features/today.md/fuel.md/me.md in the same change, and delete todayScope.test.ts once the boundary it guards no longer exists.
design: Compare frontend/src/features/today/components/TodayRow.tsx (accessory: tick|button|chevron|none, derived by logic/rowAccessory.ts) against frontend/src/shared/ui/ItemRow.tsx (the incumbent). Decide which shape wins, or whether both survive as intentionally different idioms -- that decision itself may warrant a short ADR.

Teendő: (1) finishWorkout kapja meg ugyanazt az üres-session guardot (üres → 'skipped'), (2) döntés + adatjavítás a meglévő sorra, (3) FE: a 'Edzés lezárása ✓' CTA jelezze, ha nincs logolt szett.

title: Heti zóna-kontextus: a 'zóna alatt' szöveg félrevezető, ha a heti terv már fedezi a MEV-et
description: A prep-képernyő WeekZoneCard 'below' hintje mindig azt írja: '↓ a zóna alatt — még N szett hiányzik a héten', pedig a 'below' státusz csak a KÉSZ + MA szetteket nézi (weekZone.ts:94). Ha a heti meso-terv már tartalmazza a hiányzó szetteket a hét későbbi napjaira, ez ellentmond a mezociklus-szerkesztő 'Heti szet-büdzsé' kártyájának, ami ugyanarra a csoportra '✓ optimális zónában'-t ír (élesben: Bicepsz terv 10 szett = 83%, MEV 8 → büdzsé-kártya zöld; hétfő reggel kész 0 + ma 4 → prep-kártya 'még 4 szett hiányzik'). Fix: a 'below' ág váljon szét — ha a heti terv eléri a MEV-et, semleges szöveg a hét hátralévő terv-szettjeiről; ha a teljes heti terv sem éri el a MEV-et, marad a figyelmeztetés (ez az eset egyezik a büdzsé-kártya 'under' szintjével). Feature doc: docs/features/train.md.

title: Recept logolásakor a hozzávalók mennyisége szerkeszthető legyen (ingredient overrides)
description:
Ma a LogMealSheet egyetlen lapos sorként logol egy receptet: a makrók a recept rollupjából jönnek, servings-szel osztva, és a hozzávalók láthatatlanok. Ha a valóság eltér a recepttől (a banán fele akkora, mint amivel a receptet készítettem; ma kimaradt a mandulavaj), nincs mód korrigálni — a naplózott kcal/makró és a mezo pont is a papírformát tükrözi.

Cél: logoláskor a recept kártyája inline kibontható legyen a hozzávalók listájára, ahol soronként állítható a mennyiség (natív egységben, tizedessel, 0 megengedett). Az értékek a TELJES receptre vonatkoznak ('ahogy elkészítettem'); az adag-léptető változatlanul marad mellette ('ennyit ettem belőle').

Tárolás: új nullable jsonb oszlop a meal_item-en (recipe_overrides), csak a módosított sorokkal (delta), önleíró módon (pantryItemId, name, unit, originalAmount, amount). A snapshot makrók a módosított készletből fagynak be — a recept későbbi szerkesztése nem írja át a múltat. A recipeFacts() és a snapshotNova is override-tudatossá válik, különben a mezo pont hazudik.
design: Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-recipe-ingredient-overrides-design.md (commit 4adac844). Key decision: override keyed by lineOrder WITH pantryItemId as a consistency check — recipe_ingredient has no unique (recipe_id, pantry_item_id) so pantryItemId alone is ambiguous, and lineOrder alone would silently mis-apply after a reorder. Storage: nullable meal_item.recipe_overrides jsonb, delta only, self-describing (name/unit/originalAmount). Macros, recipeFacts and snapshotNova all consume the same override map. Single-formula rule: extend RecipeMapper with an override-aware rollup rather than re-deriving the arithmetic in MealService (mezo-8xy round-per-line-then-sum + unrounded perServing are load-bearing).
acceptance_criteria: Override nélkül a logolás számai bitre változatlanok. Override-dal a snapshot makrók, a Facts (rost/cukor/só/telített zsír) és a snapshotNova is a módosított készletből számolódnak. 0-ra állított hozzávaló mindháromból kiesik. Ismeretlen vagy a recepten kívüli pantryItemId SystemMessage hibát ad. servings>1 esetén az override a teljes receptre értendő, majd osztás. FE mindkét módban zöld, a sheetben látszó szám egyezik a mentettel.

title: LLM audit: generation cost_usd is 0.00 (not null) when a priced model meets an all-null token block
description: GeminiUsageExtractor honestly normalizes absent usage to null token counters, but LlmLogWriter.applyCost then calls computeGenerationCost with a non-null (priced) snapshot + all-null tokens, and LlmPricingService.perMillion(unit,null)->ZERO, so cost_usd stores a fabricated 0.000000 on a SUCCESS row whose usage block was absent. A cost report summing cost_usd silently under-counts those rows. Fix: when the record has no usage (all token counts null / no billableChars), set cost_usd = null, not 0 — for both the generation and embedding paths. Then the ADR 0014 honesty sentence ('unknown -> null, never fabricated 0') becomes literally true. Verify via -Dmezo.test.use-testcontainers=true. Part of mezo-2zyu final-review fix wave.
notes: Fixed in mezo-2zyu final fix wave (commit c78825e9): LlmLogWriter.applyCost nulls cost_usd via hasGenerationUsage guard when no billable tokens; embedding path already guarded; ADR/companion un-hedged. Verified RED->GREEN via Testcontainers (LlmLogWriterIT).

title: LLM audit: cancelled/aborted SSE streams record no audit row (CallStatus semantics)
description: A CHAT_STREAM turn only records on doOnComplete/doOnError. If the SSE client disconnects (cancel), neither fires -> no llm_log_history row, yet Google still billed the tokens generated so far. Needs a CallStatus/lifecycle decision (e.g. a CANCELLED status recorded on doOnCancel/doFinally) — deferred from mezo-2zyu Task 4 as a separate semantic decision.
close_reason: CANCELLED CallStatus + widened ck_llm_log_history_status (202608021100 changeset); GeminiCompanionLlm.stream records on doOnCancel with partial answer + tally usage, CAS-guarded exactly-once. Merged to main b619b8ee (PR #113).

title: LLM audit: thoughts/cached tokens lost on tool-round turns (Spring AI cumulative Usage drops native metadata)
description: On any turn where Spring AI executes >=1 tool round, GoogleGenAiChatModel recurses and UsageCalculator.getCumulativeUsage returns a plain DefaultUsage with nativeUsage=null (bytecode-verified). GeminiUsageExtractor therefore cannot read thoughtsTokenCount/cachedContentTokenCount on those turns -> they record as NULL (honest: unknown, not zero). prompt/candidates/total remain correct (cumulative). Consequence: cost under-estimates the thinking slice on the priciest multi-round turns. Adapter-side capture is impossible (Spring AI discarded it); fix needs per-round capture via a ChatModel ObservationHandler or accepting the limitation. Blocks nothing in mezo-2zyu v1 (recorded null, documented in GeminiUsageExtractor javadoc).
close_reason: Root cause deeper than reported: Spring AI 2.0 tool loop lives in ToolCallingAdvisor and returns only the LAST round's response — every counter under-recorded, not just thoughts/cached. Fixed with GeminiRoundUsageAdvisor (ordered inside the loop) summing per-round native usage into a request-context GeminiRoundUsage tally; adapter prefers the tally, tool_rounds now populated (N-1). Merged to main b619b8ee (PR #113).

title: Real-device push spike — VAPID keypair + kubeseal + iPhone (MANUAL, Daniel)
description:
N1's exit criterion is unmet until this runs: no push has ever reached a real device. NOT agent-doable — needs cluster access and a physical iPhone.

Steps (full commands in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-push-n1-delivery-spine.md Task 12):
1. openssl: generate a P-256 keypair; public = 65-byte uncompressed point base64url, private = 32-byte scalar base64url. Never commit vapid-private.pem; delete it after sealing.
2. Private half -> the existing mezo-app SealedSecret as VAPID_PRIVATE + the backend Deployment env (the GEMINI_API_KEY precedent, ADR 0008).
3. Public half -> the GitHub repo VARIABLE VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC. Without it the deployed bundle ships a blank key and the page shows the honest 'vapid-missing' error (deploy.yml already plumbs the var).
4. Install the PWA to the iPhone home screen (Web Push does not work in a Safari tab), open /me/ertesitesek, enable, tap 'Teszt ertesites kuldese'.

DIAGNOSIS NOTES:
- A bad/empty PRIVATE key fails loudly: 500 WEBPUSH_SIGN_FAILED in the backend log.
- A bad PUBLIC key does NOT fail loudly — it is spliced raw into the 'k=' header and returns a generic status-mapped FAILED, indistinguishable from a transient failure. If the test push reports sent:0 and the log does NOT say SIGN_FAILED, suspect the public key first.
- WebPushClient logs the mapped WebPushResult with a scrubbed message (a push endpoint is a capability URL and is never logged in full).
- On success: N1 done, N2 (mezo-h4wp.6.2) unblocked. On failure: capture the WebPushClient log line BEFORE changing anything.
notes:
INFRA DONE 2026-07-29 — steps 1-3 complete and verified end to end. Remaining: step 4 only (Daniel, on the phone).

title: Harden jsonb records against field renames (ignoreUnknown) — root fix for mezo-1vzr
description:
Follow-up to mezo-1vzr (prod NaN incident). Root release-bug: dc040749 (mezo-eujg) renamed pal->neat + added fields on TdeeBootstrapJson, but the record had no tolerance for the OLD persisted shape and no data migration. On boot the new backend read the stale goal.tdee_bootstrap {…,pal,…}, Jackson threw UnrecognizedPropertyException (FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES) -> CrashLoopBackOff. The GoalReevaluateRunner self-heal could NOT run because the crashing read is the very read it needs. Fixed in prod by nulling the stale jsonb (see mezo-1vzr); this issue is the permanent code fix.

SCOPE: ~18 typed jsonb payloads share the same latent landmine, none currently tolerant. Notable: TdeeBootstrapJson, GoalPrescriptionJson, MealBreakdownJson, MealProvenanceJson, ProvenanceEnvelope, QuestTargetEnvelope, VolumeRecomputeJson, RunningBlockStructure, MicroFact, ActivityExtract, BriefingContentEnvelope, ChallengeRefsEnvelope, MemoirAnchorsEnvelope, LevelUpResult, MedicationCycleJson, Mesocycle volumeRecompute.

DECISION (discuss trade-off):
 Option 1 — per-record @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) on every jsonb record. Explicit, surgical, does NOT relax inbound API DTO strictness. Repetitive (~18 spots), easy to forget on the next new record.
 Option 2 — configure ONLY Hibernate's JSON FormatMapper with a dedicated lenient ObjectMapper (fail-on-unknown=false) via a FormatMapper bean / hibernate.type.json_format_mapper. One place, auto-covers all present+future jsonb, and (crucially) leaves controller/request-body deserialization STRICT. Preferred if wiring is clean in Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate 7.
 AVOID: global spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=false — also loosens inbound API DTOs (silently ignores client typos).

Key lesson: ignoreUnknown tolerance is the enabler that makes the re-evaluate self-heal runner actually work across a jsonb schema change; without it the runner is dead on arrival. Also add a regression IT: persist an old-shape jsonb row, boot context / read entity, assert no crash + fields null. Consider documenting a 'jsonb schema-change checklist' (tolerant read + migration/re-eval) in docs/references/liquibase_conventions.md or a small ADR.

title: Systemic: in-tx DataIntegrityViolation catch-and-reread is broken on Postgres (RitualService/HabitService/QuestService)
description:
Found by the R2 final whole-branch review (feat/daily-closing-ritual): the shipped race-guard pattern — saveAndFlush inside @Transactional, catch DataIntegrityViolationException, re-read in the SAME tx — cannot work on Postgres: the constraint violation aborts the tx (25P02), the re-read throws on the aborted connection, and commit would raise UnexpectedRollbackException anyway. The race loser gets a 500, not the intended idempotent 200.

=== REPRODUKALVA (2026-08-14), es a hatokor NAGYOBB a jelentettnel ===

Bizonyitva, nem feltetelezve:
- TxRaceGuardReproIT izolalja a mechanizmust: az in-tx ujraolvasas 'current transaction is aborted' hibaval elszall; kulon tranzakciobol viszont mindig sikeres.
- RitualServiceRaceIT (2 szal, CyclicBarrier, 5 kor): a javitas elott koronkent PONTOSAN EGY hivas bukott (5/10) — determinisztikus, nem flaky.

UJ RESZLET, amit az eredeti jelentes nem vett eszre: a hibat dobo utasitas az INSERT, nem a SELECT. A persistence context meg tartja a bukott entitast, igy az ujraolvasas auto-flush-a ujra kiadja az insertet a megszakadt kapcsolaton — vagyis a catch blokkban BARMELY repository-hivas elszall, nem csak az adott tabla olvasasa.

NEGY hely, nem harom (a 4. nem volt a jelentesben):
1. RitualService.insertOrReread — JAVITVA (commit d74e96ee), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + ujraolvasas.
2. HabitService.ensureRows — javitva (insertMissing, unnest + ON CONFLICT), de a keres a 4. helyen hal meg.
3. QuestService.getDay lazy-generate — hatravan.
4. HabitCatalogService.ensureCatalog (:46-54) — UJ. Ugyanaz a torott minta; a HabitServiceRaceIT-ben ez a bukó insert (habit_chain).

KET javitasi alak kell, nem egy:
- 1-3: egy tablaba szurnak -> nativ INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. FONTOS: a conflict-target ismetelje meg az index predikatumat (where is_deleted = false), mert az uq_* indexek PARCIALISAK.
- 4: ket tablat seedel lancolva (habit_chain -> habit_def, ~13 oszlop JSON seedbol) -> a bootstrap kulon beanre emelve REQUIRES_NEW propagacioval; a belso tx bukasa nem erinti a kulsot. Kovetkezmeny, amit dokumentalni kell: sikeres esetben kulon commitol, tehat a seed bent marad, ha a kulso tx kesobb visszagordul (seed-adatnal ez rendben van).

Also: correct FeaturesConfiguration.RITUAL_SWITCH javadoc ('no ritual beans' -> repository stays for the evaluator) + habit.md 9 gotcha line about switch-off leaving evening_ritual forever pending.

title: Train: cannot start another weekday's workout today (e.g. Thursday's session on Friday)
description: The whole gym start chain is keyed to the calendar day. GET /api/train/workouts/today (WorkoutService.getToday -> findPlannedTemplateForDate) resolves the template day by matching TODAY's HU weekday label only; ActiveWorkoutPage (/train/session) is driven solely by useWorkoutToday(); GymDaySheet gates its CTA on day.current ('Nézet-mód · csak a mai napot lehet indítani'); TrainTodayPage hero + WeeklyDayRow only offer start on today. Note: POST /api/train/workouts/start is already day-agnostic (accepts any owned templateSessionId, dates the instance LocalDate.now()), but even a forced start would be invisible: getToday would still resolve today's weekday -> null/other day and never surface the open instance. Fix needs (a) getToday (or a param'd variant) to surface ANY open instance dated today and resolve exercises off instance.templateSessionId, plus completedToday keyed to date-not-template; (b) FE entry point (GymDaySheet footer 'Indítsuk ma' on non-today, non-completed days; maybe weekly rows); (c) decide done-marking semantics (weekDoneDates is instance-date based, so doing Thursday's plan on Friday marks Friday done — likely correct).
notes: Implemented on feat/cross-day-workout-start (PR #25). Variant A + D1-D6 approved via browser mockup (artifact 40eaec9d, 2 rounds). BE: getToday day resolution open>param>label, week-scoped completedWorkout, startWorkout 409 guards (TRAIN_WORKOUT_OPEN_ELSEWHERE / TRAIN_DAY_DONE_THIS_WEEK), WorkoutSummaryResponse.templateSessionId. FE: GymDaySheet 4-state footer, /train/session?day= param. Tests: CrossDayWorkoutIT (7), GymDaySheet.test.tsx (7), FE 1198/1198 both modes. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-17-cross-day-workout-start-design.md. Follow-up: mezo-j3x0 (Mai tab rows + rest-day hero resume).

title: [bug] MedicationApiIT.testLogDose_…_whenPostedToday flaky: fails before 07:00 UTC
description: testLogDose_shouldReturn201AndStartCycle_whenPostedToday sets administeredAt to LocalDate.now(UTC).atTime(7,0). When the suite runs before 07:00 UTC (09:00 CEST), that timestamp is in the future and the medication future-date guard returns 400, failing the test. Time-of-day-dependent flake from mezo-d94. Fix: use a today timestamp that is never in the future (start-of-day UTC), preserving the 'today → retaDay 1' semantics. Surfaced while running P3b (mezo-lmox) gates at 04:46 UTC.
notes: Fixed in f64fa89: administeredAt now start-of-day UTC, never future.

title: Fix iOS overscroll/rubber-band at top of the app scroller
description: On installed PWA / iOS Safari the user can drag the page downward at the very top, rubber-banding the .screen-content scroller (and chaining to the viewport), revealing empty space. Root cause: .screen-content (the single app scroller) has no overscroll-behavior set, so the browser default permits the boundary bounce + scroll-chain. Fix: overscroll-behavior-y:none + -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch on .screen-content, plus overscroll-behavior:none on html,body as belt-and-suspenders. CSS-only, frontend/src/styles/prototype.css.

title: Quarantine FE mock seed to mock mode: real-mode dual-mode hooks must never fall back to the static seed (cold-load flash)
description: Root-cause class behind mezo-yew. Four dual-mode hooks use a default-param fallback to the STATIC mock seed that also fires in REAL mode while the query is loading (initialData is undefined in real mode, so data is undefined until resolve → the '= mockSeed' default kicks in): pantryHooks.ts:16 (= mockData), recipeHooks.ts:17 (= mockRecipes), fuelHooks.ts:33 (= seedDayData), weightHooks.ts:37 (= mockWeightTrends). Effect: on a cold load / hard refresh in real mode the user briefly sees FAKE seed data (mock recipes/pantry/day/weight-trend) before their real data loads. Daniel always tests live with his own data, so he hits this flash. The '= []' hooks (weightLog, sleepLog, goals) are already safe (empty, not seed).
design: Invariant: REAL mode NEVER returns mock seed — unresolved query → an EMPTY/zero value (or a loading skeleton), never the seed. Recommended: a shared useDualQuery<T>(key, { mock, mockData, realFetch, realEmpty }) helper that bakes in initialData: mock ? mockData : undefined, staleTime: mock ? Infinity : 0, and data: q.data ?? (mock ? mockData : realEmpty). Migrate the 4 leaking hooks (+ optionally the safe ones for consistency) to it; pass a realEmpty per hook ({ingredients:[],stash:[]} / [] / zero-targets FuelDay / neutral WeightTrends). Components already tolerate empty (Kamra/recipe empty states). Optional follow-on: expose isPending so views can show skeletons instead of an empty flash. Keep mock-mode behavior byte-identical (synchronous initialData for parity/tests).
close_reason: Shipped: useDualQuery helper enforces 'real mode never returns the mock seed' (realEmpty, never seed during the loading window). Migrated usePantry/useRecipes/useFuelDay/useWeight(trends); already-safe hooks untouched. Durable guard test (dualMode.guard.test.ts) fails the build if the leaky '{ data = seed } = useQuery' pattern reappears anywhere in src (sibling-tolerant regex). Shared pct() 0/0->0 helper (MacroHero + LogMealSheet). bd memory dual-mode-read-invariant saved. Adversarial review clean after 2 fix rounds. FE 605/605 both modes, build clean. Merged 0d70a7f, deployed.

title: Recipe-arm meal-log contribution rounding: converge backend double-round vs FE single-round
description: Meal-logging (mezo-arb): a recipe-arm meal_item's displayed contribution can be ±1-3 kcal off the persisted value. E.g. 1000kcal/3 servings ×2 -> backend 666, FE 667. Cosmetic + self-correcting (getDay refetch repaints the server value) but mock!=real on the recipe arm. Converge all 3 sites onto ONE convention (recommend: drop the backend per-serving scale-0 round so the snapshot keeps precision -> single-round everywhere = the more accurate value; OR double-round the FE to match the stored whole-number snapshot). Pantry arm is already exact parity.

title: Goal upsert: validate targetDate >= startDate (G3 timeline 500 on inverted dates)

title: Run builder: reconcile weeks scalar with structure.weeks.length (single source + mock fixtures)
description: Follow-up from Task 7 code review (mezo-9pv). RunningBlockBuilder tracks draft.weeks (scalar) and draft.structure.weeks.length independently; addWeek/removeLastWeek + the Math.min/max(8/1) clamp keep them in sync ONLY when they start synced. Real-backend data is always consistent (newDraft builds N weeks; create/update persist the full structure), so production is unaffected. But the Phase-1 mock fixtures are inconsistent: running.ts rb-archived-01 (weeks:8 / structure.weeks:1) and rb-planned-01 (weeks:6 / structure.weeks:1) — opening them in mock mode renders N week chips of which all but week 1 show 'Ez a hét nincs a tervben'. Fix: (1) make the mock fixtures consistent (structure.weeks.length === weeks), and (2) derive the week-chip count + add/remove gates from draft.structure.weeks.length as the single source of truth, recomputing the weeks scalar from the structure on save, so the counter/gates/editor can never disagree. Also minor a11y: give the auto-save indicator role=status/aria-live=polite. Not blocking the redesign merge.

title: Date-aware deeplink for cross-midnight deferred intervention cards
description: Intervention cards generated between quiet-hours start and midnight defer their push to next-day quiet-hours end (AnchorResolver.interventionFireMinute), but the card's own message_date stays the generation day. GET /api/proactive/feed?date= only returns the LOCAL today's rows, so the deep-linked /today?n=<id8> push from a next-morning push cannot surface the card on /today — the 'Segitett?' verdict chips are unreachable for that card. Fix: make the deeplink/feed lookup date-aware (e.g. resolve by card id directly, or have /today accept a date param and fetch across the boundary) so a deferred card's chips are reachable from the push that announces it. See docs/features/_platform-notifications.md sec 3d (mezo-b3pp.19 final-review finding 2).

5. ProfileProperties.renderMaxTokens has @Min(50) while PROFILE_HEADER alone costs 48 tokens — only 2 tokens of headroom for the prose at the floor. Not violated today, but a longer header would leave zero. Consider raising the floor.

title: Graph reinforcement bump may permanently saturate pattern-node edges toward 1.0
description:
Follow-up from mezo-b3pp.10's final whole-branch review (GraphMaintenanceService final review, 2026-08-23).

PatternDetectionService writes a fresh 'snapshot' pattern_event for a confirmed pattern on essentially every nightly run where the pair's gate verdict is LIVE — not just when something changed. GraphMaintenanceService.reinforceFreshPatterns treats any snapshot from the last 24h as 'fresh evidence' and bumps every edge touching that pattern's promoted node by graph.reinforcement-bump (default 0.05), capped at 1.0.

Arithmetic: nightly decay removes 0.01 x weight; reinforcement adds a flat 0.05. The bump wins at every weight in [0,1] (5x at w=1.0, 25x at w=0.2). So every edge touching a promoted PATTERN node ratchets to the 1.0 cap within roughly ten nights and stays there as long as the pattern keeps snapshotting. Since these are the hub nodes GraphEdgeStructurer hangs most edges off, graph.prune-floor can never reclaim them and traversal's weight ordering degenerates toward a flat 1.0 tier for the busiest part of the graph.

This matches spec section 6.5 literally ('fresh pattern evidence bumps its node's edges +0.05 capped at 1.0') and is not a bug in the current slice — CompanionProperties.Graph's own javadoc frames the bump as decay's 'counterweight', which implies balance rather than saturation though.

Worth revisiting once the graph has run for a while (lived-with evidence, same spirit as the W2 gate decision). Two candidate fixes if the ratchet turns out to be unwanted:
1. Require the snapshot to differ materially from the previous one before counting as 'fresh' (PatternDetectionService.recordSnapshot already loads the previous snapshot for its band-crossing check, so the signal is close at hand).
2. Scale the reinforcement bump by (1 - currentWeight) so it decays as the edge approaches the cap, rather than applying a flat bump.

Files: backend/src/main/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/companion/graph/service/GraphMaintenanceService.java (reinforceFreshPatterns), backend/src/main/java/io/mrkuhne/mezo/feature/companion/service/PatternDetectionService.java (recordSnapshot / the nightly snapshot-write cadence).

title: PatternDetectionServiceIT.testDetect_shouldFreezeUserJudgedRow_whenConfirmed flakes on a 1-microsecond timestamp compare
description:
Seen red in CI run 32490814082 (PR #223, W4.1):

  expected: 2026-08-21T14:17:54.590441Z
   but was: 2026-08-21T14:17:54.590442Z
  at PatternDetectionServiceIT.java:269

A one-microsecond difference — the test asserts an exact Instant equality across a Postgres round trip, so it is at the mercy of microsecond rounding/truncation. Unrelated to the change under test (W4.1 touches no pattern-detection code); it just happened to land in that run.

Fix: compare with a tolerance (assertThat(actual).isCloseTo(expected, within(1, ChronoUnit.MILLIS))) or truncate both sides before comparing, rather than asserting raw Instant equality.

title: CompanionFeedbackApiIT: no case for unknown verdict / unknown reason / empty ids / >200 ids
description:
W4.1 (mezo-b3pp.15) documents this as a known gap in docs/features/companion.md §8. CompanionFeedbackApiIT's contract-validation coverage is artifactKind ONLY (testPutFeedback_shouldReturn400_whenArtifactKindUnknown, testListFeedback_shouldReturn400_whenKindUnknown). Nothing pins:
- PUT with an unknown verdict value
- PUT with an unknown reason value
- GET with an empty ids list (contract minItems: 1)
- GET with >200 ids (contract maxItems: 200)

All four are enforced by the generated CompanionFeedbackApi's bean-validation annotations rather than hand-written code, so a contract regression would ship green. Four cases in the existing IT close it. Related: mezo-b3pp.23 (the >200 case is the same territory as the header-size limit).

title: Unread MezoChip dot can re-appear on an already-read thread
description:
Cosmetic bug, low reachability. In TodayPage.tsx (~line 326-327), the unread-dot logic is:

  const latestId = messages.length > 0 ? messages[messages.length - 1].id : null
  const msgsUnread = latestId != null && latestId !== seenId

messages comes from buildMezoMessages({ briefing, note, briefingDemo }) (features/today/logic/mezoMessages.ts), which pushes at most two entries with FIXED ids: 'briefing' (if a briefing exists) then 'note' (if a same-day CompanionNote exists), in that order. latestId is simply the id of the last pushed entry — 'note' when a note is present, else 'briefing'.

Repro sequence:
1. Both a briefing and a companion note exist for today. Thread's latest id is 'note'.
2. User opens MezoMessagesSheet -> openMessages() calls markMessagesSeen(date, 'note') and setSeenId('note') (shared/lib/seenMessages.ts). Dot clears.
3. Later in the SAME day, useCompanionNote() (data/today/heartbeatHooks.ts or equivalent) starts returning null again — e.g. a nudge/closing note's time window closes, or a refetch drops it for any other reason (the hook is not guaranteed monotonic within a day).
4. buildMezoMessages now only pushes the briefing entry. latestId flips back to 'briefing'.
5. msgsUnread = ('briefing' !== 'note') = true -> the coral unread dot re-appears on MezoChip even though nothing new was said and the user already read everything that's currently showing.

Root cause: the unread comparison keys off a small FIXED id ('briefing'/'note') rather than a value that is monotonic/stable across a note appearing-then-disappearing within the same day (e.g. a count, a hash of the thread content, or "seen" tracked per-id-that-existed rather than "seen == single latest id").

Suggested fix directions (not prescriptive): track a set/count of seen ids instead of a single latestId scalar, or don't let the unread signal go from false back to true within the same day once the note that produced 'note' disappears (only compare against ids that are STILL present, or treat a shrinking thread as never re-arming unread).

Non-goals: this is UI-cosmetic only, no data loss, no write-path involved. Low priority (P3) - the note transitioning from present to absent within the same day is an edge case (proactive heartbeat notes are typically time-window-gated, not click-to-dismiss), but it IS reachable, e.g. mock scenario switches or a real-mode refetch racing a window boundary.

Found during the mezo-e26w today-ios-redesign fix wave pre-merge review (2026-08-12). Files: frontend/src/features/today/pages/TodayPage.tsx:319-334, frontend/src/features/today/logic/mezoMessages.ts, frontend/src/shared/lib/seenMessages.ts.

title: Stale darwin visual goldens: train-gym + train-session drift on main

notes: Investigated 2026-08-08 (PR #157): only train-session light+dark still drifted (train-gym re-baselined by a later commit). Root cause: darwin goldens predated the Heti zóna-kontextus prep card (live-zone-unify) + mezo-oyhy.3 estimateSessionMinutes pill change (~78 -> ~53 perc). The ['train','weekWorkouts'] 'No queryFn was passed' console error is benign: dev-only React Query useBaseQuery warning for the intentional enabled:false queryFn-less cache observer in weekMuscleLogHooks.ts (fires on observer mount even when disabled; never fetches). Measured with Playwright's own comparator: the 78->53 digit swap = 305 diff px on darwin (>120 tolerance) but <120 on linux — so the LINUX train-session golden still carries the stale ~78 pill and CI stays green; it will fold into the next legit linux regen.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #157 (merged b33c8940): regenerated darwin train-session goldens; train-gym had already been re-baselined. Full darwin suite 40/40. queryFn console error confirmed benign (dev-only observer warning). Linux train-session golden still carries the tolerated stale ~78 pill — folds into next legit linux regen.

title: Extract the duplicated exercise-identity resolution (3 copies)
description: Follow-up from the medal-collection final review (mezo-wp6n, PR #110). The exercise-identity resolution block ('c:'+catalogId else 'n:'+name, over findIdentityRowsIncludingDeleted, plus the catalog display merge) now exists verbatim in THREE places: ExerciseRecordService, MedalService, and GymSignalCalculator. Identity semantics are a load-bearing invariant - soft-deleted day-edit rows must still count, or a plan edit silently erases history - and it now has to be changed in three files in lockstep. Extract into one resolver (feature/train/service/ExerciseIdentityResolver) consumed by all three. Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by the medal work; the medal slice made it a three-way rather than two-way duplication.
