WorkoutReviewPage renders WorkoutSummary without a medals prop, so /train/review/:workoutId has neither the medal block nor the 'N medál' title suffix - a past workout's review is silent about what it earned, while the live summary right after finishing shows them. Not a regression (it never passed hadPR either) and the /train/medals cabinet covers the history, but the review page is where you would look for one specific session. Needs WorkoutDetailResponse to carry medals[] (MedalService.forSession already computes exactly this), then pass them through.

title: Medal XP: SESSION_VOLUME records pay prBonusXp into max_strength
description: Follow-up from the medal-collection final review (mezo-wp6n, PR #110). ProgressionService.applyGym counts all four RECORD-tier medal types into recordMedalCount, so a SESSION_VOLUME record pays prBonusXp (40) into max_strength. Volume climbs weekly by design in an accumulation block, making SESSION_VOLUME the most frequently firing record type - so most exercises earn one most weeks, landing ~6x40 XP of volume-driven bonus in a strength skill. Two problems: max_strength is semantically the wrong skill for a volume record, and the single pr-bonus-xp knob cannot be tuned down for volume without also devaluing WEIGHT/E1RM. This matches the spec exactly (2026-07-30-medal-collection-design.md sections 6 and 7.3) so it is a design consequence, not drift, and the economy is display-only.
design: Options: (a) exclude SESSION_VOLUME from recordMedalCount; (b) give it its own smaller property and route it to a volume-ish skill; (c) leave it and accept faster max_strength progression. Decide by watching whether max_strength levels start outpacing the other athletic skills.

title: Make the NOVA-freeze test actually discriminate (it passes against the pre-fix code too)
description:
MealOverridesIT.testCreate_shouldKeepTheFrozenNova_whenAnOverrideOnlyChangesAnAmount (added in mezo-ormb's final fix wave) asserts the right value but cannot fail against the pre-fix implementation. The pre-fix code ran dominantNova() whenever ANY override existed; since the test never drifts pantry data between recipe-save and meal-log, that live read lands on the same max(1,4)=4 the frozen novaDominant holds. Both implementations pass.

To make it discriminate, soft-delete (or edit the nova of) the high-NOVA pantry item AFTER creating the recipe and BEFORE logging: DELETE /api/pantry/{id} is a soft delete (is_deleted = true), so the recipe_ingredient FK RESTRICT does not block it, and dominantNova's findAllById + @SQLRestriction then cannot resolve that row. Expected: pre-fix -> NOVA 1 (the live read loses the deleted syrup); post-fix -> NOVA 4 (the frozen novaDominant is kept because no line was dropped to 0). Verify the mutation by temporarily reverting MealService's anyLineDropped ternary to overrides.isEmpty() and confirming the test goes red.

Related: mezo-6xnf (freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient) would make this whole class of drift impossible.
notes: Correction: the sibling issue referenced in this description as 'mezo-6xnf' is actually mezo-4tzf (freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient). The wrong id was a guess that also landed in commit bd37511c's message and cannot be corrected there without rewriting main's history.

title: Freeze per-line NOVA on recipe_ingredient so a logged meal's snapshotNova never depends on live pantry rows
description:
Found by the mezo-ormb final whole-branch review. MealService.buildItem picks snapshotNova as: overrides.isEmpty() ? recipe.getNovaDominant() (FROZEN at recipe-save) : dominantNova(recipe, overrides) (LIVE pantry_item.nova via findAllById, which @SQLRestriction filters for soft-deletes). recipe_ingredient stores no per-line nova, so the live read was forced.

mezo-ormb narrowed the trigger: the live recompute now runs only when a line is actually dropped to 0 (that is the only case where the SET of contributing ingredients changes, so the only case where the dominant NOVA can move). A non-zero amount change now keeps the frozen value. That removes the 'an unrelated override flips nova semantics' bug.

Residual: if a line IS zeroed AND another line's pantry row was since soft-deleted or had its nova edited, the recomputed dominant still reflects live data rather than what was eaten. Fix properly by adding recipe_ingredient.snapshot_nova (captured in RecipeService.buildLine alongside the other snapshot* fields) and computing the dominant from the frozen per-line values in BOTH branches.
acceptance_criteria: snapshotNova on a logged meal is derived only from values frozen at recipe-save time; editing or soft-deleting a pantry item afterwards cannot change any already-logged meal's snapshotNova, with or without overrides.
notes: Note: commit bd37511c's message and PR #107 originally referenced this issue as 'mezo-6xnf' — an id guessed before the real one was read back. THIS (mezo-4tzf) is the real issue; the commit message is immutable on main.

title: [flake] ActiveWorkoutPage.test.tsx real-mode tests time out locally (5000ms) — reproduces on clean origin/main
description:
Surfaced while verifying mezo-ormb. 'VITE_USE_MOCK=false pnpm test ActiveWorkoutPage' fails on this machine with vitest 5000ms test timeouts. Verified on a clean origin/main checkout (7ec9e81a) in an isolated worktree: it fails there too, so it is NOT caused by any feature branch. The failing subset varies run to run (2 failed/65 passed on one run, a different single test on another), which is the signature of timing sensitivity under machine load rather than a logic defect. All failures are in the file's real-mode group (e.g. 'real mode: a hard reload on /train/session resumes instead of redirecting while queries load', ActiveWorkoutPage.test.tsx:756).

Worth deciding: raise testTimeout for that file's real-mode group, or make the queries deterministic so the test does not depend on wall-clock. CI (clean ubuntu-latest) may or may not reproduce it — check a recent ci.yml 'Tests (real mode)' leg before investing.

title: Expose the recipe line's frozen per-basis rate so the FE can mirror the backend exactly on overridden lines
description:
Surfaced by the mezo-ormb Task 6 review. The backend computes every recipe line from RecipeIngredientEntity's FROZEN snapshotPer/snapshotKcal/... captured when the recipe was last saved; there is no re-snapshot mechanism. The frontend cannot see those values — RecipeIngredientResponse exposes only 'contribution' (the already-rounded macro share AT the line's stored amount) and no per-basis rate.

mezo-ormb mitigated most of the exposure: computeRecipeMacrosWithOverrides now reuses the server-frozen 'contribution' for every UNTOUCHED line. But an OVERRIDDEN line has no frozen rate on the wire for its new amount, so it is rescaled from the LIVE pantry row. If that pantry item's macros changed after the recipe was saved, the log sheet's preview for that one line disagrees with what the server freezes on save.

Fix: add the frozen per-basis rate to RecipeIngredientResponse (contract-first) — 'per' (snapshotPer), 'basisUnit', and the per-basis macros — map them in RecipeMapper.toIngredientResponse, carry them into the FE RecipeIngredientLine type and recipeApi.fromResponse, populate them in the mock seed's enrichLine, then have computeRecipeMacrosWithOverrides scale overridden lines from the frozen rate instead of the live pantry row. Deriving an implied rate from contribution/amount is NOT a valid shortcut: 'contribution' is already rounded to whole numbers, so it loses precision (snapshot 110/100g at 3 g -> contribution 3 -> implied 1.0/g -> at 6 g gives 6, while the backend gives 7).
acceptance_criteria: An overridden line's previewed macros equal what the backend freezes, even when the referenced pantry item's macros changed after the recipe was last saved. Covered by a test that drifts the live pantry row and asserts the overridden line still scales from the frozen rate.
notes: Final-review widening (mezo-ormb): the blast radius is bigger than 'the preview can differ when macros drifted'. When an overridden line's pantry row is UNRESOLVABLE (soft-deleted — PantryService.deleteItem has no in-use guard), the FE previewed that line as 0 while the backend still scales it from the recipe's frozen snapshot and never consults the pantry at all. mezo-ormb mitigated this by rescaling the wire's frozen 'contribution' in that fallback, which is lossy (the frozen value is pre-rounded) but far closer than 0. The full fix is still to put the frozen per-basis rate on RecipeIngredientResponse so an overridden line scales exactly like the server.

title: Notification preview copy mirrors hardcoded minutes instead of the resolved anchor
description: After the N2 fix wave moved memoir/midday/weekly anchors past their generator's cron (prose-generation-grace-min: 15), two frontend spots still hardcode the OLD minute: NOTIFICATION_CATEGORY_META's memoir description ('Vasarnap este 19:00' — the anchor is now 19:15) and notificationForecast.ts's MIDDAY_HHMM / MEMOIR_HHMM mirrors. The sparkline buckets by hour so only the memoir sub-line and the dense-window minute labels are off by 15 minutes; nothing sends at the wrong time (the backend anchor is authoritative). Deliberately NOT fixed in the wave: re-hardcoding a now-config-derived minute into Hungarian user copy would recreate exactly the duplication FIX 2 removed. Proper fix: serve the resolved anchor minute to the FE (e.g. include it in the pref response, or a small GET that returns today's due-time list) and let the sub-lines + forecast read it, so there is one source of truth for the minute.

title: Train Mai polish follow-ups from the mezo-9bbc final review
description:
Three residual items parked at the end of mezo-9bbc's final review (all Low, none blocking that merge):

1. dayStripItems' isToday is still flag-based (features/train/logic/dayStripItems.ts, reads d.isToday). After mezo-9bbc made TrainTodayPage's isTodayShown date-based, a real-mode rest or run-only day now correctly renders 'Mai nap' while NO DayStrip chip is marked MA, wears the coral .today border, or says '· ma' in its aria-label. Same class of bug as the fixed one, one surface further out.

2. Latent mock-only date trap: TrainTodayPage omits the sheet date when shownIso === todayIso, and the mock sport mutation then falls back to localDateString(). If the mock fixture's flagged 'today' (Csü) ever gains a sport slot, that log would be dated the real weekday and the card would not flip to MEGVAN. Unreachable today (no Csü sport slot; the schedule mutation is a mock no-op).

3. Stale comments at TrainTodayPage.tsx (around the todayRow/isTodayShown derivation and the DayStrip selected fallback) still claim shownDay can be undefined on a real-mode rest day. The C2 calendar fallback made that impossible, so they describe a dead path and the selected={... ?? DAY_ORDER[todayIdx()]} fallback is unreachable.

Also noted: I1 (cross/TRX tone on Heti rows) ships with no visual-golden coverage, because the mock week's sport slots carry no sport discriminator so every slot resolves to volleyball. A mock fixture with a cross or TRX slot would give the golden suite teeth there.

title: RecipeEditorPage draft state seeds once, before a cold real-mode load resolves
description: RecipeEditorPage seeds its whole draft (name, slot, starred, servings, prep/cook, tags, lines and - since mezo-uavr - role) from useState first-render initializers reading editing = recipes.find(id). On a cold real-mode deep link to /fuel/recipes/:id/edit the ['recipes'] query has not resolved on first render, so editing is undefined and every field seeds to its default; when the list lands, the guard's 'Nincs ilyen recept.' fallback goes away but the draft stays blank. Today the whole draft is blank in that state (so it is visibly wrong rather than silently wrong) and the page is normally reached by navigation from the detail page with a warm cache - which is why this was accepted as pre-existing rather than a mezo-uavr regression. Fix the pattern once for the whole form: either block the editor render until the recipe resolves, or re-seed from editing in an effect keyed on its id. Found during mezo-uavr Task 7 review.

title: Mock recipe seed has no post_workout recipe
description: frontend/src/data/fuel/mockRecipes seeds role: 'pre_workout' (rec-1 / the MSW recipeFixture) and 'standard' everywhere else, so the 'Edzes utan' role label never renders in mock mode - not the detail hero chip, not the library card tag, not the PONTSZAM rubric note ('edzes utani merce szerint'), not the editor's third segment in a seeded-edit state. Mock mode is the offline demo + the both-modes test surface, so a whole third of the mezo-uavr feature is invisible there. Also inconsistent: seed rec-2 / rec-4 are slot/tag-labelled pre-workout yet carry role standard, which reads like a bug to anyone browsing the seed. Fix: give one seed recipe role: 'post_workout' and align the pre-workout-labelled seeds with their role. Found during mezo-uavr Tasks 6 and 8 review.

title: PRE_WORKOUT prose prompt invites blaming protein
description: RecipeBreakdownProseService.java:126-127 ends the PRE_WORKOUT role block with '(a feherje/zsir-dominancia itt gyengebb illeszkedes)'. That phrasing invites the LLM to write protein down as a fault, contradicting the pre-existing macro rule elsewhere in the same prompt ('tobblet-feherjet sose rodd fel hibakent'). The honest framing of the same fact is scarcity-of-carbs, not excess-of-protein: 'keves a szenhidrat a szerephez'. Deterministically the score is identical either way (the pre_workout macro target is carb-heavy, so a protein/fat-dominant recipe scores lower under it) - this is purely about the prose not blaming the wrong nutrient. Update the copy and the RecipeBreakdownProseServiceTest assertion that pins it. Flagged in mezo-uavr Task 5 review as 'fix in a later wave'.

title: a11y: Fuel segmented controls need radiogroup semantics
description: The SLOT segmented row (pre-existing) and the new SZEREP segmented row in frontend/src/features/fuel/pages/RecipeEditorPage.tsx are plain buttons: no role='radiogroup' on the container, no role='radio' + aria-checked on the options, and no aria-pressed fallback. A screen reader announces three unrelated buttons with no indication of which one is selected, and there is no arrow-key roving-tabindex navigation. Same defect on both controls, so fix them together (and check the other segmented rows in Fuel/Train while there: the typebar in FuelRecipesPage, LogMealSheet's slot row, AiLogSheet's slot row). See the accessibility-patterns skill for the radiogroup/roving-tabindex recipe. Found during mezo-uavr Task 7 review.

title: Pantry writes must invalidate the recipe-derived caches
description: usePantryActions.invalidate() (frontend/src/data/fuel/pantryHooks.ts:52) only invalidates ['pantry']. A pantry macro edit therefore silently changes every recipe's deterministic fit + template breakdown server-side (RecipeBreakdownService recomputes on read and regenerates the prose when the numbers no longer match) while the FE keeps serving the ['recipes'] / ['recipeBreakdown'] caches until they happen to refetch. Two consequences: (1) the recipe library badge + the detail score sheet show a pre-edit fit; (2) the mezo-uavr refreshing flag never fires for this path, so the honest 'Mezo ujraertekeli a receptet...' banner is skipped and the stale prose swaps in silently on the next refetch. Fix: add qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['recipes'] }) and qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['recipeBreakdown'] }) to the pantry write invalidation (mirroring useRecipeActions, which already invalidates ['pantry']). Then correct the recipeHooks JSDoc, which currently states this path is NOT an invalidation, and docs/features/fuel.md. Found during mezo-uavr Task 9 review.
notes: Shipped in PR #93 (merge 2393713e, live v0.139.1). Scoped twice over: only the recipes whose lines reference the edited item, and only when a fact the scorer re-reads live changed (NOVA, fiber/sugar/salt/sat-fat, category, basis) — a recipe's macros are frozen in its line snapshots, so a price or kcal edit moves nothing. delete always invalidates referencing recipes; add/import touches no recipe cache. Query keys extracted to data/fuel/queryKeys.ts (the invalidation is mutual).

title: Fuel Layer C: goal-engine + Me TDEE reconciliation (dynamic maintenance)
description: Follow-up to mezo-1oy5 (spec §10, out-of-scope there). The Fuel daily budget is now dynamic (BMR×NEAT + Σ MET activity + balance) but the goal-engine (TdeeBootstrapService/GoalProjectionService) + the Me 'Alap-TDEE' card still use static BMR×PAL. title: [bug] Recipe editor: a line for a since-deleted pantry item shows UUID + 0 macros (seed snapshot name/contribution into DraftLine)
description: Pre-existing (predates mezo-yew, surfaced by the adversarial review of that fix). In RecipeEditorView edit mode, a recipe line whose pantry item was soft-deleted no longer resolves against usePantry().ingredients → row renders line.refId (UUID) + contributionOf(line, undefined)=0, and zero-drags the live MAKRO-OSSZEG. The data to fix this already exists: the backend persists snapshotName + snapshot macros on recipe_ingredient, and recipeApi.fromResponse carries them onto RecipeIngredientLine.name/.contribution — but the editor's DraftLine seed (RecipeEditorView.tsx ~line 79) discards both. Fix: carry name (and contribution) into DraftLine, and fall back to the snapshot name when usePantry() resolution misses; the live editor cannot recompute contributions for a missing ingredient, so for a deleted item show the frozen snapshot contribution at the stored amount (and consider disabling the stepper for that orphan line). value: A conflicted (CONFLICTING) GitHub PR runs NO pull_request CI checks at all — GitHub cannot build the test-merge ref, so 'gh pr checks' reports 'no checks reported'. macOS git-hook gotcha: GNU 'timeout' is NOT installed on this machine, so the beads pre-commit/pre-push hooks run 'bd hooks run' WITHOUT a timeout guard. If multiple bd processes contend for the Dolt lock (e.g. bd init's own commit colliding with manual git commits), the hook hangs INDEFINITELY and git commit/push silently stalls. Fix when it happens: kill the stuck 'bd hooks run' + 'bd export' processes (ps aux | grep bd) to clear the lock, then retry — a single serialized commit works fine. Permanent fix: brew install coreutils and put its gnubin on PATH so 'timeout' exists.

db8 hit a real bootstrap failure: MealRepository extends OwnedRepository<MealEntity> (brief-mandated for the date-ordered family), but the inherited findAllOwned JPQL orders by e.date — a field MealEntity lacks (it has loggedAt/mealDate). On Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate 7, derived+@Query queries are VALIDATED EAGERLY at context startup, so the invalid inherited query fails bean creation ('Query validation failed for select e from MealEntity e ... order by e.date asc') even though nothing calls it. The brief assumed an uncalled-but-inherited invalid query is harmless; under eager validation it is not. FIX faithful to brief intent: override findAllOwned in MealRepository with a @Query valid for MealEntity (order by mealDate asc, loggedAt asc), keeping 'extends OwnedRepository' exactly as mandated. The override stays unused by the service (it uses the day-finder) — it exists only to give the family a MealEntity-valid query.

DUAL-MODE READ INVARIANT (mezo-0xl): real mode must NEVER return the FE mock seed — not even transiently during the query's loading window. The footgun is 'const { data = mockSeed } = useQuery(...)': the destructuring default fires whenever data is undefined, which INCLUDES the entire real-mode load, so it flashes Phase-1 demo data onto a live user's screen (this is the same bug class as mezo-yew). ALWAYS use the useDualQuery helper (frontend/src/data/useDualQuery.ts) for a dual-mode read whose mock side is a static literal: useDualQuery({ queryKey, mockData, realFetch, realEmpty, realStaleTime? }) returns data: q.data ?? (mock ? mockData : realEmpty) — real mode gets realEmpty (empty/zero), never the seed; mock keeps synchronous initialData + staleTime Infinity for parity. An empty-literal default (= [] / = {}) is also safe. A guard test (frontend/src/data/dualMode.guard.test.ts) FAILS THE BUILD if the leaky '{ data = seed } = useQuery' pattern reappears in any src/data hook. Migrated hooks: usePantry ({ingredients:[],stash:[]}), useRecipes ([]), useFuelDay (zero FuelDay), useWeight weightTrends arm (zero trend). Already-safe hooks (train/running/goal/biometric/sleep + weightLog) use '?? []'/'?? null'/isPending and were left as-is. Consumer corollary: components dividing by a target/count must guard 0/0 (MacroHero now does → 0%), because realEmpty can be a zero value. Canonical doc: docs/features/_platform-data-layer.md §'The no static fallback in real mode rule' + the useDualQuery paragraph in §4.

DEPLOY GOTCHA: never put [skip ci] on the HEAD commit of a push to main — GitHub natively skips the whole workflow run when the push's head commit message contains [skip ci]. The deploy.yml triggers on 'push: branches:[main]' (no paths filter) and the version job also has if:!contains(head_commit.message,'[skip ci]'). Project convention: bd-chore/close commits normally do NOT carry [skip ci] (they deploy fine). When merging a slice + closing its bd issue, make the LAST pushed commit a non-[skip ci] one (the merge commit, or a clean trigger), otherwise the deploy is suppressed. Only the workflow's own auto-release commit uses [skip ci] to break the loop.

SB4/Spring Security 7 backend gotchas (found in Slice-A auth): (1) TestRestTemplate moved to org.springframework.boot.resttestclient.TestRestTemplate (artifact spring-boot-resttestclient, transitive via spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test) and requires @AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate to register the bean under RANDOM_PORT. (2) NimbusJwtEncoder cannot infer the JWS alg from a symmetric ImmutableSecret -> must pass JwsHeader.with(MacAlgorithm.HS256) via JwtEncoderParameters.from(header, claims), else 'Failed to select a JWK signing key'. (3) JWT resource server needs spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server (not in Initializr defaults; brings Nimbus JOSE). (4) The plan's SecurityConfig DSL (csrf(c->c.disable()), oauth2ResourceServer(o->o.jwt(j->{}))) is valid as-is on SS7. (5) SB4 ships Jackson 3: packages are tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper/JsonNode (NOT com.fasterxml.* — only jackson-annotations 2.x remains under com.fasterxml); JsonNode.asText() is deprecated, use asString(); exceptions are unchecked. (6) openapi-generator 7.17.0 'spring' generator works on SB4 with useSpringBoot4=true + useResponseEntity=false (emits @ResponseStatus from the first 2xx code, @Valid on interface params); generated com.fasterxml @JsonProperty annotations are honored by Jackson 3. Contract gotchas: NotBlank has no OpenAPI equivalent (required + minLength:1 -> Size -> VALIDATION_INVALID_VALUE, not REQUIRED_FIELD); prefer pattern over enum on request fields (invalid enum fails Jackson deser -> 500, pattern fails bean validation -> 400). IDE language server does not index target/generated-sources/openapi -> api.dto/api.controller 'cannot be resolved' diags are noise, Maven is truth.

Sheet CLOSE animation gotcha: setting el.style.animation='none' + transition + transform in ONE sync tick makes the browser coalesce the writes and JUMP to the end state (instant disappear) instead of animating — Chromium-headless tolerated it but real browsers (e.g. Safari) did not. FIX in requestClose(): animation='none'; void el.offsetHeight (force reflow to commit current pos as start frame); set transition; then set transform:translateY(100%) inside requestAnimationFrame (next frame). Verified gradual ease-out curve 0->460px over ~300ms. Entrance slide-up is a pure CSS @keyframes (sheet-rise) so it never had this problem. LESSON: when verifying animations in Playwright, sample the transform at MULTIPLE timestamps to confirm a gradual curve — a single mid-sample at full height can mask an instant jump (it fooled me once).

Egy mezociklus heti nap-beosztásának átrendezése (élő DB) = CSAK a workout_session.day_label + order_index UPDATE-je a template sorokon (template_session_id IS NULL, date IS NULL). Az exercise sorok a workout_session_id FK-n függnek, nem a napon, így a gyakorlatok/set-ek maguktól követik a napjukat; a day_label-en nincs unique constraint, tehát egy körkörös permutáció is elmegy egyetlen UPDATE-tel köztes érték nélkül. A naptári nap feloldása futásidőben történik (WorkoutService.findPlannedTemplateForDate: HU_DAY_LABELS[dayOfWeek]), tehát az UPDATE azonnal hatályos. Külön kell viszont gondolni a gym_schedule_slot-ra (day_of_week -> gym időpont), ha a PIHENŐnapok helye is változik, különben lesz edzésnap időpont nélkül.

Git workflow (single-dev --no-ff): run 'git pull --rebase' BEFORE 'git merge --no-ff <branch>', NOT in the push step after. The Session-Completion 'git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push' sequence, when run after a local --no-ff merge, replays the merge+close commits and FLATTENS the --no-ff bubble into linear history (happened on mezo-ksh/dh6/8xy/cki — work correct + pushed, but bubbles lost). Correct order: checkout main → pull --rebase → merge --no-ff → push (no second pull). If origin truly moved before push, use 'git pull --rebase=merges' to preserve the bubble.

Spring AI 2.0.0 (mezo backend): the tool-execution loop is NOT in GoogleGenAiChatModel — it lives in ToolCallingAdvisor (order MIN_VALUE+300) in the ChatClient advisor chain, re-entering everything below it once per round; ChatModelCallAdvisor (order MAX_VALUE) calls the model. Consequences: (1) the caller's final ChatResponse is the LAST round's response only — nothing merges usage across rounds (UsageCalculator.getCumulativeUsage is effectively dead code on this path, and it builds DefaultUsage with nativeUsage=null anyway); (2) tools only execute if the prompt options are ToolCallingChatOptions — DefaultChatClientUtils builds request options from chatModel.getOptions().mutate() and silently drops tool callbacks on a plain ChatOptions builder, so a stub ChatModel in tests MUST override getOptions() to return ToolCallingChatOptions or the loop never runs; (3) per-round native usage (thoughts/cached) is capturable by a custom CallAdvisor/StreamAdvisor ordered between the two (mezo uses GeminiRoundUsageAdvisor + a request-context GeminiRoundUsage tally, see mezo-58ig).

Builder shell layout (prototype.css): the global .sticky-top breadcrumb sits inside .screen-content which already has padding-top:54px (status bar) / env(safe-area-inset-top) (PWA). So .sticky-top MUST use top:0, NOT top:54px/env(...) — a non-zero top double-counts the offset and pins the breadcrumb ~54px below the status bar, letting the following header scroll over it (looks 'szétcsúszik'). Also .tab-bar is position:absolute + translucent; content scrolls behind it, so its background needs HIGH opacity (rgba(10,15,20,0.92), not 0.75) or bright content (teal CTA) bleeds through. Fixed in mezo-49j.

mezo mockups: 'the design system' to Daniel = the Deep Current notched-chamfer motif (clip-path octagon corners on chips/buttons/cells + hard SQUARE dots like .tag .dot). Plain border-radius rounded corners / circular dots read as OFF-system and get rejected. Cards in mockups should use the chamfer (borderless fill, like .tag/.macro-cell), not border-radius. Source CSS: docs/design/ux-component-library-v2.html + ux-screen-mockups-v2.html.

PhoneFrame (.phone in prototype.css) is a DESKTOP-ONLY preview mockup sized to iPhone 17 Pro Max (440x956, island 124x37, home bar 134x5). A media query (max-width:519px OR display-mode:standalone/fullscreen/minimal-ui) strips the bezel/island/fake-statusbar/home-indicator and goes full-bleed with env(safe-area-inset-*). index.html viewport uses viewport-fit=cover. So on real phones the OS chrome is used, not the mockup.
